sights.description: Villa built in 1925 in Tsujido, Fujisawa, a representative Japanese-Western eclectic building by Arata Endo.

sights.name: Joryu-ji
sights.description: Near Enoshima and known as a famous place for plum blossoms.

sights.name: Jinkoji Cave Tomb Group
sights.description: Kofun-period cave tomb group; about five tombs are currently confirmed.

sights.name: Kawana Goryo Shrine
sights.description: Said founded in 941; enshrines Prince Sawara and Kamakura Gongoro Kagemasa for calamity protection, studies, exams, and calligraphy.

sights.name: Endo Mahoroba no Sato Fujisawa Ebine and Yamayuri Garden
sights.description: Leisurely stroll a woodland where 130 wild plant species, like calanthe, goldband lily, and mountain hydrangea, bloom in turn.

sights.name: Funajizo Park
sights.description: Built for an old woman the Hojo clan killed after she taught them to drain surrounding marshes.

sights.name: Shonandai Cultural Center Children's Museum
sights.description: Complex with a large globe, hands-on world toys and ethnic instruments, a planetarium, and dome movies.

sights.name: Oba Castle Ruins Park
sights.description: Green park with many cherry trees, wisteria, about 110 roses, a play plaza, and a castle-site square.

sights.name: Hikichi River Green Space (Tenjin Bridge)
sights.description: Frog sculptures are installed on Tenjin Bridge. Rare creatures inhabit the Hikichi River flowing beneath this bridge.

sights.name: Kashiyama Inari and Itsukushima Senjinriki Benten Shrine
sights.description: Said to grant blessings for good harvests, business prosperity, community safety, and household safety.

sights.name: Iseyama Park
sights.description: A park overlooking Fujisawa city, Enoshima, and Sagami Bay.

sights.name: Fujisawa-juku Exchange Hall
sights.description: Opened in 2016 with local exhibits, a Fujisawa-juku diorama, 3D CG, and year-round events.

sights.name: Koshin-do
sights.description: A Buddhist hall of the Koshin faith in Fujisawa City, Kanagawa Prefecture.

sights.name: Kuramae Gallery
sights.description: A new art space opened in 2006 in the main house and storehouse of a rice shop built in 1929.

sights.name: Kinsazan Kannon Hall
sights.description: On a hill along National Route 467 near the Fujisawa Bridge intersection. Commonly called Obitoki Kannon.

sights.name: Former Inamotoya Kimono Shop
sights.description: A registered tangible cultural property and a representative prewar kimono merchant of Fujisawa.

sights.name: Yaku Shrine
sights.description: A shrine with a deity divided from Kawasaki Daishi in 1884, enshrining a god against epidemics.

sights.name: Hakusan Shrine
sights.description: Reached by stone steps to the left, past house eaves from the Enoshima road.

sights.name: Joko-ji
sights.description: Jodo temple in Fujisawa. Amida Nyorai is a city Important Cultural Property; the temple forest is a city natural monument.

sights.name: Shogon-ji
sights.description: Koyasan Shingon temple opened in 1184; principal image Fudo Myoo; houses Yoshitsune's memorial tablet.

sights.name: Eisho-ji
sights.description: Jodo Shinshu temple in Fujisawa; graves of innkeeper Komatsuya Genzo and women sold to inns.

sights.name: Legendary Yoshitsune Head-Washing Well
sights.description: After Yoshitsune's 1189 death, legend says villagers washed his head in this well and built a mound.

sights.name: Myozen-ji
sights.description: Nichiren temple in Fujisawa founded in 1504; Makita family graves of former official inn keepers stand there.

sights.name: Shintoku-ji
sights.description: Ji sect temple in Fujisawa; main hall ceiling has flowers and birds by priest-painter Yoshikawa Kiyoshi.

sights.name: Chosei-in
sights.description: A Ji-shu temple in Fujisawa. The current main hall was completed in 1991.

sights.name: Sanno Shrine (Fujisawa)
sights.description: Fujisawa-juku's first guardian shrine, enshrined near former Fujisawa High School in Kan'ei (1624-44) and moved here in An'ei.

sights.name: Kanno-in
sights.description: A Koyasan Shingon temple said founded by Minamoto no Sanetomo and among Fujisawa-juku's oldest temples.

sights.name: Funadama Shrine
sights.description: Said site where Kamakura's third shogun Sanetomo cut Song-bound ship timber; enshrined for safe passage and sea protection.

sights.name: Utsumochi Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Fujisawa, the oldest in Goshomi. Founding unknown; in the Kamakura period, regent Hojo Sadatoki donated the shrine hall.

sights.name: Shonan Port Lighthouse (Hot Road filming location)
sights.description: Filming location of the movie Hot Road and one symbol of Enoshima, visited by many tourists.

sights.name: Fujisawa City Fujisawa Ukiyo-e Museum
sights.description: Museum of ukiyo-e on Fujisawa-juku and Enoshima, with rotating local-material exhibitions.

sights.name: Nihon University College of Bioresource Sciences Museum (Bone Museum)
sights.description: University museum open to the public, renewed in 2019 to show bone diversity, wildlife, livestock, and pet skeletons.

sights.name: Katase Suwa Shrine
sights.description: Near Enoshima in Fujisawa; enshrines a god and consort, called a power spot for marital harmony.

sights.name: Fujisawa City Art Space
sights.description: Supports young artists, holds exhibitions, workshops, and lectures, and deepens community ties while seeking new art possibilities.

sights.name: Olympic Memorial Fountain
sights.description: Fountain pond in Fujisawa City, built to commemorate the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

sights.name: Enoshima Sea Candle
sights.description: About 59m observation lighthouse, 119m above sea, in Samuel Cocking Garden, viewing Fuji, Izu and Hakone.

sights.name: Enoshima Nakatsumiya Plaza
sights.description: Plaza between Enoshima Shrine's Hetsumiya and Nakatsumiya, known for flowers and a deck overlooking Zushi.

sights.name: Hikichi River Waterside Park
sights.description: Park along the Hikichi River with spring cherries, azaleas, and wisteria trellises, plus parking for viewing.

sights.name: Cherry Blossoms at Oba Castle Ruins Park (Fujisawa City)
sights.description: Castle ruins park among trees, with spring cherry blossoms and play equipment for a relaxed family day.

day_to_day.name: Tawara Furusato Park Soba Restaurant Shinonome
day_to_day.description: Sells morning-picked produce. Handmade soba from waterwheel stone-milled flour; soba-making experience by reservation.

day_to_day.name: Kanai Sake Brewery
day_to_day.description: The only sake brewery in Hadano City, Kanagawa, founded in Meiji 1, applying tradition to modern brewing.

day_to_day.name: Hadano Specialty Products Center
day_to_day.description: Shop at Odakyu Hadano Station's north exit selling Hadano souvenirs and tourism-association-certified local specialties.

day_to_day.name: Kitahara-do Confectionery
day_to_day.description: Founded in 1950, this long-established Japanese sweets shop keeps tradition and tries new sweets.

day_to_day.name: Kamaka Shoten
day_to_day.description: Long-established Hadano peanut shop; the next-door cafe serves rich soft serve using local peanuts.

day_to_day.name: Hadano Ito Farm
day_to_day.description: Grows vegetables, blueberries, and sweet potatoes at the foot of Tanzawa in Hadano.

day_to_day.name: Hadano Jibasanzu
day_to_day.description: Shop selling Delicious Hadano Water, first among Japan's 100 famous waters, and carefully farmer-grown Soshu peanuts.

day_to_day.name: Tomoshibi Shop Yume Sanpo
day_to_day.description: Shop where you can taste Delicious Hadano Water, first among Japan's 100 famous waters.

day_to_day.name: Ishishoan Handmade Soba
day_to_day.description: Shop serving Hadano soba born from Hadano soil and water.

day_to_day.name: Hadano Ichinoya
day_to_day.description: Hadano restaurant since 1873, barrier-free, serving Japanese, sushi, Western food, and local game.

day_to_day.name: Soba Restaurant Shinonome
day_to_day.description: Fragrant soba and seasonal Japanese dishes with tempura in a calm, tourist-friendly setting.

activities.name: Mount Takatori
activities.description: Nature-rich summit reachable by hiking, with fine views and benches suited to lunch or rest, via a varied up-and-down trail.

activities.name: Koboyama Park
activities.description: Prefectural park of three low mountains for year-round hiking, with Fuji views from Gongen-yama.

activities.name: Hadano International Riding Club
activities.description: Relaxed horseback riding amid greenery, Mount Fuji to the northwest, and full spring cherry blossoms.

activities.name: Mount Gyojagatake
activities.description: Narrow summit once had an En no Gyoja statue, now a monument with his image. Chain sections toward Shin-Dainichi.

activities.name: Sannoto
activities.description: Summit offers a full view of the Omoteone ridge and distant Mount Fuji, plus a rest area and toilets.

activities.name: Mount Tonodake
activities.description: Most popular peak in Omote Tanzawa; a 4-5 hour climb with summit views of Mount Fuji and Sagami Bay.

activities.name: Mount Ninoto
activities.description: 1122 m peak on the Tanzawa Omoteone; one name origin is a Karako Shrine legend.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Hadano Togawa Park
activities.description: Year-round flowers against Tanzawa mountains, with summer river play, barbecue, a tea room, playground, and sports facilities.

activities.name: Omote Tanzawa Citizens' Forest
activities.description: Paths from Shijuhasse River to Kurinokibora at 908 m, with cedar and cypress plantations, broadleaf woods, shelters, and a lawn.

activities.name: Kuzuha House Nature Observation Facility
activities.description: Opened in 1998 as a nature observation base in Kuzuha Green Space, Kanagawa's first National Trust green space (1987).

activities.name: Kobo no Sato-yu
activities.description: Day-trip onsen with two springs: an outdoor bath plus indoor and private baths. Calcium-rich water warms the body.

activities.name: Meisui Hadano Fujimi-no-Yu
activities.description: Day-trip onsen with Mount Fuji views. Water from 100m down is rich in metasilicic acid, said to beautify skin.

activities.name: Hadano Tanzawa Climbing Park
activities.description: Bouldering facility in Hadano Togawa Park, plus adjacent lead and speed walls for all three sport-climbing events.

activities.name: Mount Tonodake (Yabitsu Pass Trailhead)
activities.description: Trailhead pass for Tanzawa and Oyama ridges, said to be a Warring States battlefield.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Mountain Sports Center
activities.description: Mountaineering and nature activity base in Hadano Togawa Park, with 12 rooms for camps, climbing, and recreation.

activities.name: Totonoi no Sato Hadano Yukaraku
activities.description: Day-trip onsen surrounded by Tanzawa nature, rebranded May 2025, with Hadano's only medicinal carbonated spring.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Hadano Togawa Park Minashi River
activities.description: A shallow river small children can enjoy, with a downstream section dogs can also use.

sights.name: Minamoto no Sanetomo Head Mound
sights.description: Said mound where Minamoto no Sanetomo's head was secretly buried in Hadano after his 1219 assassination. Festival each November 23.

sights.name: Izumo Taisha Sagami Branch Shrine
sights.description: 1888 branch of Izumo Taisha enshrining Okuninushi, revered as Kanto's Izumo, with a thousand-year zelkova.

sights.name: Zenba Pass
sights.description: Border pass of Hadano and Isehara, used until the Zenba Tunnel was completed in early Showa.

sights.name: Mount Nenbutsu
sights.description: Ridge mountain from Mount Kobo to Mount Takatori; Buddhist chant gatherings lasted until early Showa.

sights.name: Hadano Springs (Kobo no Shimizu)
sights.description: Hadano water ranked first nationwide for taste in the Selected 100 Famous Waters poll; spring hiking is popular.

sights.name: Ryokusui-an
sights.description: Early Showa tobacco farmhouse relocated to Hadano and registered as a national tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Mount Karasuoyama
sights.description: Overlook Hadano City beyond the Sannoto ridge and enjoy the Omoteone range, including Sannoto and Tonodake.

sights.name: Lake Shinsei
sights.description: Lake formed when the 1923 earthquake dammed Ichikizawa; a national registered monument since 2021.

sights.name: Entsu-ji Temple
sights.description: Hadano temple with a city-designated important cultural property, a wooden Eleven-Faced Kannon.

sights.name: Kokuryu Falls
sights.description: 15 m waterfall that never dries, cool even in summer. Name likely comes from a nearby prayer master's hermitage.

sights.name: Sakuradote Kofun Park
sights.description: By Hadano's Mizunashi River, 35 late-7th-century circular mounds were excavated and six preserved, among the prefecture's largest groups.

sights.name: Jotoku-in Iris Garden
sights.description: Early June to early July, naturally occurring Genji and Heike fireflies sometimes fly at night, evoking a paradise.

sights.name: Imaizumi Firefly Park
sights.description: Green park near Hadano Station with Mukaihara spring stream, protected as a firefly habitat by volunteers.

sights.name: Nakogi Terraced Rice Fields
sights.description: Selected as excellent terraced rice fields. Farmers and an NPO conserve them and offer farming exchanges, preserving biodiverse rural scenery.

sights.name: Imaizumi Meisui Sakura Park
sights.description: Built in 2005 to mark 50 years since Hadano became a city. Cherry-blossom and famous-water park for local rest.

sights.name: Maimai Spring
sights.description: Named after an ancient maimaizu well. Groundwater quality improved, so water now flows artesian from 20 meters down.

sights.name: Nanohana-dai
sights.description: Clear days give 360-degree views from Boso to Fuji, including Enoshima, Izu, and Hakone. Narrow passes have tight curves.

sights.name: Tsurumaki Hydrangea Walking Path
sights.description: A hydrangea path 20 minutes on foot from Tsurumaki Onsen Station. Rainy-season blooms stand out vividly against green fields.

sights.name: Ryujin Spring
sights.description: Upper Mizunashi River spring. A dragon-shaped rock is said to house the dragon god, where ascetics and hunters rested.

sights.name: Shirasasa Inari Shrine
sights.description: Said to be one of Kanto's three great Inari shrines. Ikkanida Spring, Hikarimo pond, free ceiling viewing, antique markets.

sights.name: Hadano Cherry Blossom Road
sights.description: About 6.2 km of cherry trees from Nishi-Otake to Horiyamashita, Kanagawa's longest, forming beautiful arches each spring.

sights.name: Dainichi-do
sights.description: Said to have been founded in 742 by Gyoki. Its 175 cm Dainichi Nyorai is a prefectural Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Shungoku Spring
sights.description: About 30 minutes uphill from Minoge bus stop along Kaname River. Soft, low-hardness spring also used as a water source.

sights.name: Higeso Falls
sights.description: Named for monk Shungoku, who had a chest-length beard and trained here. Mixed woods surround the mystical falls.

sights.name: Minoge Nature Observation Forest
sights.description: Deciduous oak forest offering spring greenery, autumn foliage, winter bare trees, birds, and animals.

sights.name: Hadano Ukiyo-e Gallery
sights.description: Gallery in Hadano City Library showing about 1,900 ukiyo-e donated in 1998 by collector Otsu Maruko.

sights.name: Hadano Municipal Miyanaga Takehiko Memorial Art Museum
sights.description: Displays Miyanaga Takehiko's diverse works, changing exhibitions about every six months.

stays.description: Accommodation in Hadano.

day_to_day.name: Hakone-Yumoto Station Shopping Street
day_to_day.description: Arcade before Hakone-Yumoto Station, the Romancecar terminus and Hakone gateway, lined with souvenir shops.

day_to_day.name: Owakudani Kurotamago Hall
day_to_day.description: Sells black eggs only available here and original souvenirs, with Mt. Fuji and volcanic views.

day_to_day.name: Kojiri Forest Parking Lot
day_to_day.description: 200-vehicle lot beside Hakone Ropeway Togendai Station for Owakudani, pirate-ship cruises, fishing, and lakeside walks.

day_to_day.name: Hatajuku Yosegi Hall
day_to_day.description: Displays and sells Hakone's traditional yosegi marquetry and holds experience classes.

day_to_day.name: Hakone Yosegi Specialty Shop Hakone Maruyama Bussan
day_to_day.description: Hakone-origin yosegi craft shop offering secret boxes, tableware, stationery, and demonstrations of making and opening.

day_to_day.name: Hakone Pass Roadside Station
day_to_day.description: Route 1 roadside station overlooking Lake Ashi and Mt. Fuji, with light meals, vegetables, and yosegi souvenirs.

day_to_day.name: Ukon Beef Hot Pot
day_to_day.description: Selected wagyu in historic beef hot pot, with Hakone's only riverside seating.

day_to_day.name: Miyanoshita Shopping Street
day_to_day.description: Retro onsen-town shopping street in central Hakone with guided strolls, Sepia Collection, and Forest Reading Room.

day_to_day.name: Amazake Tea House
day_to_day.description: Edo-founded 13th-generation teahouse beside Hakone Old Highway Museum serves sugar-free amazake and charcoal-grilled mochi.

day_to_day.name: Hakone Visitor Center
day_to_day.description: Explains Hakone nature via dioramas, panels, theater, and a glass observation lounge, with craft classes and guided walks.

day_to_day.name: Murakami Jiro Shop
day_to_day.description: Salt-pickled double cherry blossoms let you taste spring's fleeting nature year-round.

day_to_day.name: Naraya Cafe
day_to_day.description: Community hub born from Miyanoshita's 300-plus-year Naraya Ryokan, with a hot-spring foot bath.

day_to_day.name: Ueno
day_to_day.description: Shop where you can taste Lake Ashi wakasagi also offered to Hakone Shrine.

activities.name: Hakone Pirate Ship
activities.description: Three pirate ships cruise Lake Ashi, with views of seasonal nature, Mount Fuji, and an underwater torii.

activities.name: Hakone Ropeway
activities.description: Ropeway between Owakudani and Togendai stations touring Hakone from about 1,000 meters, with Mount Fuji views.

activities.name: Tenzan Tojigo
activities.description: Day-trip onsen in a quiet Sukumo River valley with baths, sauna, meals, and lodging from three nights.

activities.name: Hakone Komagatake Ropeway
activities.description: A 1,783-meter ropeway in a national park links Lake Ashi to Komagatake summit in about seven minutes, with 360-degree views.

activities.name: Hakone Lake Ashi Sightseeing Cruise
activities.description: Since 1920, regular and circular cruises link three ports, with panoramic deck views of Lake Ashi.

activities.name: Hakone Craft House
activities.description: Hands-on craft hall in Hakone Gora Park with seven making experiences and one-on-one instruction.

activities.name: Forest Adventure Hakone
activities.description: French-born outdoor park with adventure and canopy courses, about 120m zip slide, and nearby putter golf.

activities.name: Hakone Kowakien Yunessun
activities.description: Onsen theme park: swimsuit Yunessun and nude Mori no Yu, coffee bath, and Hakone's only water slide.

activities.name: Hakone-en
activities.description: Hakone resort complex for leisure, dining, and shopping, with Lake Ashi cruises and the Komagatake Ropeway departing on site.

activities.name: Hakone Yuryo
activities.description: Large day-trip onsen in Hakone Yumoto with 19 private open-air baths, among the largest in greater Tokyo, plus full meals.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Onshi Hakone Park
activities.description: Prefectural park on the former Meiji-era Hakone Imperial Villa site, overlooking Mount Fuji and Lake Ashi.

activities.name: Forest Adventure Hakone / Odawara / Yokohama
activities.description: French-born outdoor park using forest trees, where you operate safety gear and advance yourself.

activities.name: Ninja Bus Water Spider
activities.description: New amphibious bus dives into Lake Ashi for views of Hakone's outer mountains, Mount Fuji, and seasonal scenery.

activities.name: Fun Space Lake Ashi Camp Village Lakeside Villa
activities.description: Campground in Fuji-Hakone-Izu National Park with rental villa cabins, tent sites, and auto sites.

activities.name: Hakone Tozan Railway (Hydrangea Train)
activities.description: Hydrangeas bloom from mid-June along the climbing line; a reserved-seat night train passes illuminated spots.

activities.name: Hakone Mountain Bike Cruising
activities.description: Mountain bike tours through forests full of negative ions around Lake Ashi.

activities.name: Saien
activities.description: Renovated old house in Miyanoshita serving monk-made Buddhist vegetarian breakfast by reservation from 8 a.m.

activities.name: Hakuundo Tea Garden
activities.description: Said to have been started by Don'o Masuda Takashi, a tea master since Rikyu. Tea preparation and interior viewing available.

activities.name: Lake Ashi Shore (Smelt Fishing and Lunch)
activities.description: A simple natural spawning method allows more smelt to be hatched and released. Smelt swim to the shore.

activities.name: Amimoto Oba
activities.description: Eat Lake Ashi smelt caught by the owner, or fish at the attached Lake Ashi Fishing Center.

activities.name: Mount Kintoki
activities.description: Stratovolcano active from 350,000 to 270,000 years ago and the highest peak of Hakone Dairinzan.

activities.name: Kai Sengokuhara
activities.description: All 16 guest rooms have open-air baths for enjoying Hakone Sengokuhara and changing scenery.

activities.name: Hakone-en Golf Course
activities.description: Offers refreshing shots toward Lake Ashi.

activities.name: Sengokuhara Yutate Lion Dance
activities.description: Yutate kagura from 1776. Rare lion hot-water rite for health, safety, and harvest. National and Kanagawa intangible cultural property.

activities.name: Miyagino Yutate Lion Dance
activities.description: Transmitted in 1776. Lions rarely perform this hot-water rite, praying for health and harvest. Prefectural and national cultural property.

food.name: フラワーカフェ ロザージュ
food.description: Flower Cafe Rosage — cafe and cake shop in Hakone, Kanagawa.

food.name: 相原精肉店

sights.name: Sengokuhara Pampas Grassland
sights.description: Vast pampas grass on Mount Daigatake is green in spring and golden in autumn; one of Kanagawa's 50 scenic spots.

sights.name: Owakudani Park
sights.description: Sulfurous volcanic valley of white smoke and dead trees, once called Hell Valley, reached by Hakone Ropeway.

sights.name: Lake Ashi
sights.description: Hakone volcano caldera lake with pirate-ship cruises, possible reflected Fuji, and summer festival fireworks.

sights.name: Hakone Shrine and Kuzuryu Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 757 by imperial order and revered by Yoritomo and Ieyasu. Kuzuryu Shrine honors Lake Ashi's guardian deity.

sights.name: Hakone Gora Park
sights.description: Japan's first French-style formal garden, over 110 years old, with symmetrical fountains, seasonal flowers, and roses.

sights.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
sights.description: Open-air museum showing about 120 masterpieces by modern and contemporary sculptors against Hakone mountains.

sights.name: Hakone-en Aquarium
sights.description: Forest aquarium with saltwater and freshwater halls, a 1,255-ton seawater tank, otters, penguins, and Baikal seals.

sights.name: Hakone Glass Forest Museum
sights.description: Displays Venetian glass that captivated Renaissance European royalty, plus Italian dining and an imported glass shop.

sights.name: Hakone Shrine
sights.description: Shrine founded in 757 beside Lake Ashi, revered by samurai for luck, wish fulfillment, and traffic safety.

sights.name: Hakone Museum of Art
sights.description: Oldest Hakone museum, opened 1952 in Gora. Japanese ceramics plus moss, maple, and rock gardens, a national scenic site.

sights.name: Hakone Karakuri Museum
sights.description: Museum of Hakone yosegi works by master craftsmen. Visitors can touch trick pieces and make boxes, coasters, or banks.

sights.name: Hakone Lalique Museum
sights.description: Sparkling jewelry and glass works by French craftsman Rene Lalique, spanning his lifetime.

sights.name: Pola Museum of Art
sights.description: Opened 2002 in Hakone. Impressionist to 20th-century Western paintings and contemporary art; seasonal forest trails.

sights.name: Pola Museum of Art: A New Eye - Monet and 21st Century Art
sights.description: Exhibits all 19 Monet oils, Asia's largest collection, plus 18 contemporary artist groups, through April 2027.

sights.name: Moto-Hakone Old Highway Cedar Avenue
sights.description: Said to be planted in 1618, cedars up to 350 years old line 500 meters of the old highway.

sights.name: Hakone Checkpoint
sights.description: Edo-period checkpoint restored using period techniques from 1983 materials. Adjacent museum and Mount Fuji views from the lookout.

sights.name: Hakone Botanical Garden of Wetlands
sights.description: Japan's first wetland plant garden in Hakone Sengokuhara, with about 1,700 species blooming through the seasons.

sights.name: Tsubaki Line (Tsubakidai)
sights.description: One of Kanagawa's 50 scenic spots, a hill on the camellia-lined Tsubaki Line, best February to April.

sights.name: Mount Taikan
sights.description: On the Yugawara-Hakone border, with views of Mount Fuji and Lake Ashi. Said to be named after Yokoyama Taikan.

sights.name: cu-mo Hakone
sights.description: A 2020 Sounzan Station spot with a viewing terrace, free foot bath, and sweets shop.

sights.name: Hakone Sekisho Travel Story Museum
sights.description: Beside Lake Ashi cruise pier and Hakone Checkpoint; cedar avenue is walkable. Serves homemade 100-percent soba.

sights.name: Okada Museum of Art
sights.description: Shows about 450 artworks from ancient to modern Japan, China, and Korea, with a seasonal garden and footbath cafe.

sights.name: Lake Ashi Skyline
sights.description: A toll road spanning Kanagawa and Shizuoka prefectures, famous for Mount Fuji views.

sights.name: Narukawa Art Museum
sights.description: On Lake Ashi in Hakone, opened 1988, focusing on contemporary Japanese painting with over 4,000 works.

sights.name: Hakone Samurai Village Museum
sights.description: Displays Edo-to-Kamakura armor, helmets, matchlocks, swords, and paintings; armor dressing in Hakone Sengokuhara.

sights.name: Hakone Geomuseum
sights.description: Museum where you can encounter the mysteries and appeal of Hakone's unique volcanic terrain.

sights.name: Hakone Ekiden Museum
sights.description: Introduces 100 years of Hakone Ekiden history from the first race in 1920, with race topic videos inside.

sights.name: Choan-ji
sights.description: Popular for autumn leaves and 500 Arhat statues; a flower-rich Soto Zen temple with purple iwashajin blooms around October.

sights.name: Miyagino Hayakawa Embankment Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: About 120 Somei-Yoshino trees line about 600m of the Hayakawa embankment; peak late March to mid-April.

sights.name: Hakone Museum of Photography
sights.description: Permanent Mount Fuji photographs by Hakone photographer Kei Endo; opened in 2002 in Gora.

sights.name: Mount Komagatake
sights.description: Only Hakone view of seven Izu islands, Suruga and Sagami bays, plus Fuji and the outer rim.

sights.name: Nicolai Bergmann Hakone Gardens
sights.description: Unique Hakone gardens by Danish flower artist Nicolai Bergmann, combining nature and flower art, with seasonal blooms and a cafe.

sights.name: Hiryu Falls
sights.description: Kanagawa's largest waterfall, falling 15 then 25 meters; Kamakura-period ascetics trained beneath it.

sights.name: Honma Yosegi Art Museum
sights.description: Museum of traditional Hakone yosegi since the Edo period, with about 500 works and 200 on display.

sights.name: Hakone Kuzuryu Forest
sights.description: Lush nature park by Lake Ashi with wild trees and flowers, Hakone Kuzuryu Shrine, a nature trail, and lawns.

sights.name: Hakone Old Highway
sights.description: Part of the early Edo Tokaido over Hakone Pass; west-slope stone pavement was laid in 1680.

sights.name: Kanrei Domon
sights.description: 1931 shelter under a Great Kanto Earthquake-collapsed cliff, protecting vehicles from rockfall. National Important Cultural Property since 2015.

sights.name: Kojiri Water Gate
sights.description: Built near Ashinoko Camp Village at Sakasagawa mouth to regulate lake water level.

sights.name: Sansho Roses near Komagatake Summit
sights.description: Pale pink one-day sansho roses bloom mid-May to mid-June near Hakone Komagatake's about 1,356 m summit.

sights.name: Kousa Dogwood around Lake Ashi
sights.description: White kousa dogwood blooms around caldera Lake Ashi in June, with red fruit in September and November foliage.

sights.name: Hakone-Yumoto Firefly Park
sights.description: Fireflies restored by a local group glow in early June; now over 500, with a stream and hydrangeas.

sights.name: Shojin Pond Area
sights.description: Near Route 1's highest point on Kamakura-period Yusaka Road, with Motohakone stone Buddhas and April bean cherries.

sights.name: Chitose Bridge
sights.description: Built in 1930 with foreign tourists in mind; wave-linked newel posts; National Important Cultural Property since 2015.

sights.name: Motohakone Stone Buddhas
sights.description: Near Shojin Pond, stone Buddhas centered on 3.2m Rokudo Jizo are designated National Important Cultural Property and historic site.

sights.name: Yao Bikuni's Tomb
sights.description: Part of the Moto-Hakone stone Buddha group near Shojingaike; the surrounding area is a National Historic Site.

sights.name: Mount Kanmurigatake
sights.description: A 1,409-meter volcano in Hakone formed as a lava dome after a steam explosion and collapse about 3,000 years ago.

sights.name: Rokudo Jizo
sights.description: Late Kamakura to early Muromachi Jizo stone Buddhas and pagodas; a National Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Tada no Mitsunaka's Tomb
sights.description: A late Kamakura stone treasure-seal pagoda near Shojingaike, designated a National Historic Site and Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Mount Kamiyama
sights.description: Highest Hakone peak overlooking Lake Ashi, from Sagami Bay to Boso, with Mount Fuji views.

sights.name: Asahi Bridge
sights.description: A concrete arch bridge on National Route 1 at the gateway to Hakone.

sights.name: Twenty-five Bodhisattvas
sights.description: Stone Buddhas and pagodas are National Important Cultural Properties of medieval Jizo faith; the area is a National Historic Site.

sights.name: Graves of the Soga Brothers and Tora Gozen
sights.description: Three stone five-ring pagodas along National Route 1 toward Ashinoyu, near Shojin Pond; National Important Cultural Properties.

sights.name: Ocho Jizo
sights.description: A cliff-carved Buddha west of National Route 1 near Shojingaike, a National Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Kana Garden
sights.description: Photogenic rose garden and panorama beds, with vegetable-harvest and rice planting and harvesting experiences.

sights.name: Hiratsuka City Art Museum
sights.description: Holds special exhibitions of Shonan-related works under the theme Art and Light of Shonan.

sights.name: Yoshizawa Eight Views
sights.description: Beautiful satoyama scenery in Yoshizawa, Shonan Hiratsuka, selected to preserve for posterity.

sights.name: Tobiyatsu Hill (Majestic Mount Fuji)
sights.description: Top Fuji viewpoint among Yoshizawa Eight Views; sometimes diamond Fuji; spring embankment cherries.

sights.name: Shonan-daira (Komayama Park)
sights.description: Green park spanning Hiratsuka and Oiso; about 180m observatories offer a 360-degree Shonan panorama and famous night views.

sights.name: Hinomiya Shrine and Standing Stone
sights.description: Roughly 4-meter-square natural rock called Hinomiya-san, with a Yamato Takeru legend and counted among Yoshizawa Eight Views.

sights.name: Komyo-ji Kannon Hall (Kaname Kannon)
sights.description: Hiratsuka Eight Views and 7th Bando 33 site; Kaname Kannon's miniature shrine is a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Shogan-ji Temple
sights.description: After the stone steps, a view of the Miura Peninsula. Founded in 1502, long a Soto Zen training temple.

sights.name: Tsukagoshi Park
sights.description: Rare in the prefecture: a front-square rear-square burial mound with a cherry tree on top and good views.

sights.name: Yatsurugi Shrine and Kanman Fudo
sights.description: Guardian of Yoshizawa; large zelkova at upper shrine, nationally designated wooden Fudo statue at lower shrine.

sights.name: Myoen-ji (Tsuchiya Coin-Washing Benzaiten)
sights.description: Tendai temple in Tsuchiya, Hiratsuka, enshrining Benzaiten, with a cave and coin-washing pond.

sights.name: Tentoku-ji
sights.description: Linked to Sanada Yoichi Yoshitada of the Ishibashiyama battle; later an Ueda clan castle in Sagami.

sights.name: Tsuchiya Basket Chrysanthemum Garden
sights.description: Best viewing is from late October to mid-November.

sights.name: Hiratsuka Offshore Experiment Tower (University of Tokyo Ocean Alliance)
sights.description: Yellow observation and marine experiment tower 1 km offshore in 20 m of water, run by the University of Tokyo.

sights.name: Ishikkusu Banyu Flower Field
sights.description: Three hectares of seasonal flowers on the Sagami River riverbed: tulips, poppies, cornflowers, lavender, zinnias, and cosmos.

sights.name: Hiratsuka Hachimangu Shrine
sights.description: One of Sagami's six shrines, reputedly founded by Emperor Nintoku in 68, hosting several festivals.

sights.name: Hachimanyama Park
sights.description: Central-city oasis with cherry, roses, hydrangea, and bush clover, monuments, and a Western-style building.

sights.name: Hachimanyama Western-style House (Former Yokohama Rubber Hiratsuka Factory Memorial Hall)
sights.description: Registered as a national tangible cultural property as a historic building.

sights.name: Kirifuri Falls (Hiratsuka Eight Views)
sights.description: Hiking course around marble-like falls and a stone reportedly visited by Yamato Takeru. Also called Maou Falls.

sights.name: Shichikoku Pass and Tohara
sights.description: City's westernmost 182 m pass, said named for seven-province views. Mountain ridges and seasonal flowers welcome hikers.

sights.name: Hiratsuka Coast
sights.description: About 4 km coast. Fuji's silhouette appears behind Shonandaira TV tower, a Hiratsuka symbol. Popular year-round for views.

sights.name: Banyu Bridge Area (Shonan Itako)
sights.description: Hiratsuka waterside district called Shonan Itako, with Banyu Fureai Park, arena and soccer field upstream of Banyu Bridge.

sights.name: Yoshizawa Eight Views (Village Pond)
sights.description: Selected village landscape of the Yoshizawa Eight Views, with terraces and wooded traditional farmhouses against Mount Oyama.

sights.name: Yoshizawa Eight Views (Yoshizawa Elementary School)
sights.description: Yoshizawa Eight Views site. In spring the main gate road shows cherry trees and the school's red triangular roof.

sights.name: Yoshizawa Eight Views (Yurugi Hill)
sights.description: Selected Yoshizawa Eight Views site. A farm road from Kami-Yoshizawa Yatsurugi Shrine reveals fan-shaped terraces backed by Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Yoshizawa Eight Views (Megumigaoka)
sights.description: Selected as Yoshizawa Eight Views for local revitalization. Azaleas and dogwoods line Megumigaoka's outer road, best in late April.

sights.name: Hiratsuka City Museum
sights.description: Hiratsuka museum themed on Sagami River basin nature and culture, with a popular children's planetarium.

sights.name: Okiku Mound
sights.description: Grave site of Okiku, heroine of the Edo ghost story Bancho Sarayashiki, in Beniya-cho Park.

sights.name: Edo-guchi Mitsuke Site
sights.description: Restored Edo-side entrance of old Tokaido Hiratsuka-juku, based on a photo an early Meiji Italian minister took home.

sights.name: Hiratsuka-juku Waki-Honjin Site Monument
sights.description: Hiratsuka-juku had one honjin and one waki-honjin, auxiliary lodging for officials and daimyo.

sights.name: Official Notice Board Site
sights.description: Boards of basic shogunate or lord laws were posted here; Hiratsuka also showed fares to Fujisawa and Oiso.

sights.name: Former Hiratsuka-juku Honjin Site
sights.description: Tokaido post-town inn for daimyo, nobles, and officials; 163 tsubo, 20 sitting rooms, gate and raised room.

sights.name: Kyoto-side Mitsuke Site
sights.description: Said to be Hiroshige's Hiratsuka Nawate-michi view, with Komayama, the path, and Hanamizu River.

sights.name: Hiratsuka Mound
sights.description: Monument off the old Tokaido. Legend says Taira Masako's flat mound became the name Hiratsuka.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Environmental Science Center
sights.description: Conducts environmental survey research, monitoring, and learning support to preserve and create safe living conditions.

sights.name: Namiki Maki-e Workshop (PILOT)
sights.description: Taisho brick former naval powder factory exhibits maki-e fountain pen history and lacquer works; advance reservation required.

sights.description: Red spider lilies bloom from mid-September amid green mountains and golden rice in Hinata.

sights.name: Miharashidai Observatory (Oyama Hiking)
sights.description: A 770-meter observatory overlooking Isehara and Atsugi.

sights.name: Niju Falls
sights.description: One of Oyama's six falls, also called the rain-prayer falls.

sights.name: Oyama Temple
sights.description: One of Kanto's three great Fudo, founded in 755. Iron Fudo Myoo and two attendants are national Important Cultural Properties.

sights.name: Iyori Pass
sights.description: A pass on the old Sakamoto road connecting Hadano City and Oyama.

sights.name: Fudo Myoo
sights.description: Fudo Myoo at Iyori Pass in Tanzawa, said to have once served as a guidepost.

sights.name: Mizunomi Jizo
sights.description: Located before Iyori Pass along the Sengen-yama forest road.

sights.name: Stone Monument at the Foot of the Bridge

sights.name: Mujozan Johotsugan-ji
sights.description: Head temple of the Tendai Tansei school, opened by Priest Tansei, founder of an ascetic wandering practice.

sights.name: Fujimidai Viewpoint
sights.description: On the main trail to Oyama summit, where Mount Fuji is visible on clear days.

sights.name: Husband and Wife Cedars
sights.description: A mystical 600-year-old auspicious tree on the way up to Fujimidai.

sights.name: Isehara Daijingu Shrine
sights.description: Shrine near Isehara Station, called Daijingu-san. Setsubun festival, spring cherries, and a summer flower market.

sights.name: Sannomiya Hibita Shrine
sights.description: Heian-recorded Engishiki shrine, Sagami's third, revered by Yoritomo and Tokugawa shoguns. Holds wooden guardian dogs said to be Kanto's oldest.

sights.name: Isehara Shibuta Riverbank
sights.description: About 600 meters of moss phlox bloom along the Shibuta riverbank, a Kanagawa flower spot.

sights.name: Yamazakura at Oyama Afuri Shrine
sights.description: Four mountain cherries over 400 years old dot the back hill. Seeing all four needs about a one-hour hike.

sights.name: Okame Cherries along Oyama Shindo
sights.description: About 160 deep pink Okame cherries line 300 meters along Oyama Shindo, blooming from early to mid-March.

sights.name: Mount Oyama
sights.description: Western Kanagawa mountain popular for hiking, a six-minute cable car, and Michelin two-star views.

sights.name: Samukawa Winter Sunflowers

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Waterworks Memorial Hall

day_to_day.description: Born from a brewer's wish for junmai ginjo with the best rice and local farmers, valuing sake-food harmony.

day_to_day.description: Shop where people with disabilities and locals work together, serving meals and selling crafts and local specialties.

activities.name: Nakagawa Onsen Buna-no-Yu
activities.description: Day-trip alkaline simple onsen near Lake Tanzawa, called Shingen's hidden bath and a beauty bath.

activities.name: Mount Tonodake
activities.description: Most popular peak in Omote Tanzawa; a 4-5 hour climb with summit views of Mount Fuji and Sagami Bay.

activities.name: Nishi-Tanzawa Nakagawa Onsen Uozantei Yamabuki
activities.description: Hinoki baths over 2 meters in diameter with soft pH 10.6 water. Nakagawa Onsen, known as Shingen's hidden spring.

activities.name: Yamakita Town Health and Welfare Center Sakura no Yu
activities.description: Multipurpose facility attached to the health and welfare center. Open to the public, with spring cherry views.

activities.name: Ryugen Glass Workshop
activities.description: Rebuilt from a house left outdoors over 20 years. Visitors blow colored glass cups and collect them the next day.

activities.name: Hidamari no Sato

sights.name: Kamakura Central Park
sights.description: Central Kamakura park with greening, nature-use, and conservation zones. Somei-Yoshino bloom late March. Designated disaster evacuation site.

sights.name: Koshigoe Fishing Port
sights.description: Southwestern Kamakura fishing port landing Sagami Bay seafood, with public access and Enoshima and Mount Fuji views.

sights.name: Myohon-ji Temple
sights.description: Said to be the oldest Nichiren temple, a ten-minute walk from Kamakura Station East Exit.

sights.name: Hongaku-ji
sights.description: Founded in 1436 and donated by Ashikaga Mochiuji to Nichijitsu; called Nichicho-sama and Higashi Minobu.

sights.name: Ankokuron-ji Temple
sights.description: Founded at Nichiren's hermitage; closed cave where Rissho Ankoku Ron was written; views of Kamakura and Fuji.

sights.name: Anyo-in Temple
sights.description: Temple linked to Hojo Masako, moved here after burning in 1333, now famous for azaleas.

sights.name: Egara Tenjin Shrine
sights.description: Enshrined in the Heian period, called one of Japan's three ancient Tenjin shrines, busy with academic prayers.

sights.name: Engaku-ji
sights.description: Historic Rinzai Zen temple founded by Hojo Tokimune, with a National Treasure bell and Shariden.

sights.name: Sugimoto-ji
sights.description: Kamakura's oldest temple, founded in 734, with Eleven-faced Kannon as its principal image.

sights.name: Ofuna Kannon-ji
sights.description: Huge white Kannon temple west of Ofuna Station; statue completed in 1960 symbolizes the Ofuna district.

sights.name: Enno-ji
sights.description: King Enma, made in 1250, is the principal image; Ten Kings show judgments of sinners sent to hell.

sights.name: Amanawa Shinmei Shrine
sights.description: Shrine said founded in 710 by Someya Taro Tokitada. Minamoto no Yoritomo, Masako, and Sanetomo reportedly visited.

sights.name: Kamakura Museum of Literature
sights.description: Closed for major repairs; FY2029 reopening planned. 1936 Maeda villa with literary materials and 250 roses in spring and autumn.

sights.name: Kencho-ji
sights.description: Rinzai Kencho-ji school's head temple, first of Kamakura's Five Mountains, founded by Hojo Tokiyori; birthplace of kenchin soup.

sights.name: Jomyo-ji Kisen-an
sights.description: Jomyo-ji ranks fifth among Kamakura's Five Mountains, Rinzai Kencho-ji school. Taste matcha at Kisen-an viewing a dry landscape garden.

sights.name: Zeniarai Benzaiten Ugafuku Shrine
sights.description: Kamakura's foremost money-luck shrine where washing coins is said to increase wealth. Its spring is one of five famous waters.

sights.name: Dankazura
sights.description: Raised approach about 500m from the second torii to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, improved by Yoritomo in 1182, with cherries and azaleas.

sights.name: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine
sights.description: Guardian shrine of the Kamakura shogunate, with stone steps, sacred ginkgo trees, Masako Stone, and peony garden.

sights.name: Hasedera Temple
sights.description: Kamakura temple known for flowers year-round and a 9.18 m wooden Eleven-faced Kannon, among Japan's largest.

sights.name: Grave of Minamoto no Yoritomo
sights.description: Stone pagoda said to be Yoritomo's grave, on the estimated memorial-hall site, with Hojo Yoshitoki remains; a national historic site.

sights.name: Kotoku-in Temple
sights.description: Check the official website for the latest information.

sights.name: Hokoku-ji
sights.description: Kamakura temple with bamboo grove, dry garden, Ashikaga graves, matcha, and Sunday morning zazen.

sights.name: Kita-Kamakura Old Folk House Museum
sights.description: House over 100 years old showing Abe Akemi's permanent Showa Family dolls and seasonal exhibitions.

sights.name: Sanzagaike Forest Park
sights.description: Pond also called Kamakura Lake and a 2.4 km path; quiet cherry viewing peaks in early April.

sights.name: Kamakurayama Cherry Blossom Avenue
sights.description: Early Showa luxury housing whose aged roadside cherry trees are a famed Kamakura spot.

sights.name: Genjiyama Park
sights.description: Green park beside national historic site Kewaizaka, with a Yoritomo statue, seasonal flowers, and hiking courses.

sights.name: The Museum of Modern Art, Kamakura Annex
sights.description: Behind Tsurugaoka Hachimangu on the Kamakura Kaido, with exhibition rooms and a contemporary sculpture garden.

sights.name: Kitakamakura Yoh Shomei Art Museum
sights.description: Personal museum of picture-book artist Yoh Shomei, conceived as a beautiful picture book, displaying about 80 originals.

sights.name: Kamakura City Kaburaki Kiyokata Memorial Art Museum
sights.description: Built on Kaburaki Kiyokata's final residence site in Kamakura, holding eight exhibitions a year.

sights.name: Kamakura-bori Museum
sights.description: Only museum of Kamakura carving, displaying about 50 pieces from the Muromachi period to today.

sights.name: Toray Zelkova Avenue
sights.description: Zelkova-lined straight road in front of Toray Research Institute, with summer greenery and autumn foliage.

sights.name: Inamuragasaki
sights.description: Famous cape between Yuigahama and Shichirigahama, a scenic spot for sunsets, Enoshima views, and sometimes Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Kewaizaka Pass
sights.description: National historic site and one of Kamakura's seven entrances, a steep cut-through thought sealed in war to block enemies.

sights.name: Kamakura-gu
sights.description: Founded in 1869 by Emperor Meiji to honor Prince Morinaga at his death site.

sights.name: Komyo-ji Temple
sights.description: One of eight Jodo sect head temples, founded in 1243, with sunsets, spring cherry, and summer lotus.

sights.name: Eisho-ji
sights.description: Founded in 1636, many original buildings remain, all designated National Important Cultural Properties.

sights.name: Kaizo-ji
sights.description: Spacious front garden from the gate to the main hall shows seasonal flowers.

sights.name: Jokomyo-ji
sights.description: Founded by Hojo Tokiyori and Nagatoki; the entire precinct is a National Historic Site.

sights.name: Jochi-ji
sights.description: Built around 1281 by Hojo Munemasa's wife and son Morotoki. Has Kanro-no-i well. Lush grounds are a national historic site.

sights.name: Jomyo-ji
sights.description: Kencho-ji school temple ranked fifth of Kamakura's Five Mountains. Ashikaga family temple and national historic site.

sights.name: Engaku-ji Kigen-in
sights.description: A sub-temple of Engaku-ji within the Engaku-ji precincts.

sights.name: Yoshiya Nobuko Memorial Museum
sights.description: Female writer Yoshiya Nobuko's home, donated to the city by her wish, is a social-education learning facility.

sights.name: Kamakura Noh Stage
sights.description: Founded in 1970 near Kamakura's Great Buddha to promote Noh, with performances and mask and costume displays.

sights.name: Meigetsu-in
sights.description: Rinzai Kencho-ji temple in Kita-Kamakura built by Uesugi Norikata, known for 2,500 Meigetsuin Blue hydrangeas.

sights.name: Third Torii
sights.description: The third torii built at the entrance of Tsurugaoka Hachimangu.

sights.name: Taiko Bridge
sights.description: Stone arched bridge built in 1182, spanning the center of Genpei Pond beyond the third torii.

sights.name: Maiden
sights.description: Officially the lower worship hall. Festivals, shrine weddings, and arts offerings are held. Shizuka Gozen danced here.

sights.name: Great Ginkgo
sights.description: Also called Hidden Ginkgo. Sanetomo was reportedly killed by hiding nephew Kugyo. It fell in 2010; a young tree grows.

sights.name: Maruyama Inari Shrine
sights.description: Hilltop shrine west of the main shrine. Oldest precinct hall, from the Muromachi period, ringed by red flags for prosperity.

sights.name: Kamakura Museum of National Treasures
sights.description: Opened April 3, 1928. History and art museum exhibiting cultural properties from local shrines and temples, including open Buddhist statues.

sights.name: Hataage Benzaiten Shrine
sights.description: Shrine on an island in Genji Pond, restored in 1980. Many tie wishes to Genji flags linked to Yoritomo.

sights.name: Kaifuki Jizo
sights.description: On the hill behind Zuisen-ji, midway on the Ten-en Hiking Course. Enter from the course entrance.

sights.name: Shojoken Observatory
sights.description: You can view Sagami Bay and Kencho-ji Temple in the distance.

sights.name: Mount Ohira
sights.description: The highest peak in Kamakura City, adjoining Kamigo-cho, Sakae Ward, Yokohama City.

sights.name: Kamakura History and Culture Exchange Center
sights.description: Museum opened in May 2017 where visitors learn, experience, and exchange Kamakura's historical and cultural heritage.

sights.name: Joju-in Temple
sights.description: Temple built in 1219 atop 108 steps, overlooking Yuigahama, with hydrangeas and cherry blossoms.

sights.name: Wakamiya-oji
sights.description: Straight approach from the first torii to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, said built by Yoritomo for Masako's safe birth.

sights.name: Hibiya Kadan Ofuna Flower Center
sights.description: Botanical garden in Kamakura with seasonal flowers, a vast peony garden, roses, camellias, a greenhouse, and a cafe.

sights.name: Ichijo Ekan Villa
sights.description: Nationally designated Important Cultural Property in a strolling garden with hydrangeas, autumn leaves, red pines, and moss.

sights.name: Daibutsu Kiridoshi
sights.description: A cut pass from Kamakura toward Fujisawa with medieval cave tombs, preserving a narrow, steep old road.

sights.name: Myoho-ji
sights.description: Nichiren temple founded in 1357, also called Moss Temple for its beautiful mossy stone steps.

sights.name: Manpuku-ji
sights.description: Shingon Daikakuji-school temple built by Gyoki; Yoshitsune reportedly wrote his Koshigoe letter here.

sights.name: Hokai-ji
sights.description: Said to be built by Ashikaga Takauji to console Hojo spirits; nicknamed Bush Clover Temple.

sights.name: Koshoku-ji
sights.description: Ji-shu temple founded in 1278; Ippen laid its foundation and Sakua opened it, a nembutsu hall for about 700 years.

sights.name: Kosoku-ji
sights.description: Nichiren temple opened by Nichiro at Yadoya Mitsunori's residence, where Rissho Ankoku Ron was submitted in 1260.

sights.name: Gokuraku-ji
sights.description: Japan Heritage temple near Gokurakuji Station, with important cultural property statues, cherries, and matcha.

sights.name: Kamakurayama Shrine
sights.description: Originally Fueta farmers' guardian and fishermen's sea protector; named Kamakurayama Shrine as the housing area developed.

sights.name: Rokkokuken-yama Forest Park
sights.description: Park on the mountainside. The observation plaza sometimes offers views of Kamakura, Sagami Bay, Mt. Fuji, and Izu Oshima.

sights.name: Kuhon-ji
sights.description: Temple said built in 1337 by Nitta Yoshisada to console Hojo war dead, on his 1333 headquarters site.

sights.name: Goryo Shrine
sights.description: Shrine to Kamakura Gongoro Kagemasa, known as Gongoro-sama, famous for its September 18 masked procession.

sights.name: Kamakura Bunkakan Tsurugaoka Museum
sights.description: Museum of Kamakura history and culture in a preserved modern-art building designated a National Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Imamiya Shrine
sights.description: Shrine northwest of the main shrine, enshrined in 1247 to console three exiled retired emperors.

sights.name: Yui Wakamiya
sights.description: Kamakura shrine also called Moto-Hachiman, origin of Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, founded in 1063 by Minamoto no Yoriyoshi.

sights.name: Sasuke Inari Shrine
sights.description: Shrine with vermilion torii and white foxes, called Shusse Inari, also welcoming pet owners.

sights.name: Zuisen-ji
sights.description: Rinzai Zen temple in Nikaido, Kamakura; grounds are a national historic site and the garden a national scenic place.

sights.name: British Antique Museum BAM Kamakura
sights.description: Museum displaying authentic British antiques over 100 years old, design-supervised by Kengo Kuma.

sights.name: Ichijo Ekan Villa
sights.description: Early Edo Kyoto villa of Prince Ichijo Ekan, relocated to Kamakura; national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Kakuon-ji
sights.description: Begun in 1218 as Okura Yakushi Hall; thatched hall enshrines an Important Cultural Property Yakushi statue. No photos past reception.

sights.name: Kamakura City Kawakita Film Museum
sights.description: Opened in 2010 on the former home site of the Kawakitas for film exhibits and screenings.

stays.description: Ohmachi Junxion — lodging in Kamakura, Kanagawa.

stays.description: We Home Stay Kamakura Yuigahama — lodging in Kamakura, Kanagawa.

day_to_day.name: Kawasaki Daishi Main Approach
day_to_day.description: About 500 meters to Kawasaki Daishi; over 3 million in three New Year days; kuzumochi and daruma shops.

day_to_day.name: Domoto Seika Headquarters Factory
day_to_day.description: Factory direct shop for Daishi-maki senbei, designated a Kanagawa famous sweet and selected among 100 specialties.

day_to_day.name: Kawasaki City International Exchange Center
day_to_day.description: Promotes international understanding and cultural exchange, with multilingual information, exhibits, and a library.

day_to_day.name: Kawasaki Daishi Nakamise Street
day_to_day.description: Shops line a 200m street from Kawasaki Daishi's Daisanmon, selling Tontoko candy and kuzumochi.

day_to_day.name: Lazona Kawasaki Plaza
day_to_day.description: Large commercial facility directly connected to JR Kawasaki Station, with fashion, gourmet, cinema, gym stores, and seasonal events.

day_to_day.name: Kawasaki Korea Town (Yakiniku)
day_to_day.description: Retro, unpretentious yakiniku restaurants and Korean grocery stores line this Korea Town, locally called Cement Street.

day_to_day.name: Kawasaki DICE
day_to_day.description: Large complex linked directly to JR Kawasaki Station, with dining, shopping, and nine-screen cinema.

day_to_day.name: Kawasaki Azalea
day_to_day.description: One of Japan's largest underground shopping streets, with 150 varied shops, directly linked to Kawasaki Station.

day_to_day.name: Grand Tree Musashikosugi
day_to_day.description: Commercial facility near Musashi-Kosugi Station, opened in 2014 and renovated in 2021 under the GOOD LIFE LAB theme.

day_to_day.name: Ginryugai
day_to_day.description: Kawasaki Ward arcade linking Shinkawa Street and City Hall Street, built by filling Furukawa River to rehire the unemployed.

day_to_day.name: Hosei-dori Shopping Street
day_to_day.description: A 250m shopping street of about 100 shops from Musashi-Kosugi Station, famous for an 80m somen-nagashi contest each July.

day_to_day.name: Motosumi-Bremen Street Shopping Street
day_to_day.description: Shopping street from Motosumiyoshi Station west exit, renamed in 1990, with a 1991 friendship agreement with Bremen's Lloyd Passage.

day_to_day.name: Motosumi Oz-dori Shopping Street
day_to_day.description: Shopping street outside Motosumiyoshi Station east exit. Official character Ozuccho. Bremen shopping street is across the tracks.

day_to_day.name: Kaiju Bar (Closed)
day_to_day.description: Ultra kaiju star in this izakaya oasis for eternal boys, opening as a permanent shop.

day_to_day.name: Kawasaki City Agricultural Technology Support Center
day_to_day.description: Supports farmers' crop techniques and public participation, with pear blossoms in early April and produce sales.

day_to_day.name: Kuzumochi Honpo Sumiyoshi
day_to_day.description: A shop where you can taste Kawasaki Daishi kuzumochi.

day_to_day.name: Farm Patisserie Slow Sweets (Asao, Kawasaki)
day_to_day.description: Shop for Kanagawa strawberries, with direct sales and strawberry picking.

day_to_day.name: Domoto Motoki Main Store
day_to_day.description: Shop selling individually handmade Daishimaki senbei crackers.

day_to_day.name: Shirakawa-go Soba Restaurant
day_to_day.description: First-floor soba shop in gassho-zukuri Yamashita House, a prefectural important cultural property in the open-air museum.

day_to_day.name: Lazona Kawasaki Plaza
day_to_day.description: Station-connected mall with brands, goods, dining, events, workshops, and rest spots.

day_to_day.name: The Warehouse Business Lounge & Cafe
day_to_day.description: Lounge and cafe in Kawasaki King Skyfront Tokyu REI Hotel for light meals, drinks, rest, meetings, and work.

activities.name: Daishi Park
activities.description: Park beside Kawasaki Daishi Heiken-ji with baseball, tennis, pool, and lawn. Shenyang's 1987 Chinese garden has seasonal plants.

activities.name: Promenade along the Nikaryo Canal
activities.description: Tama River flow and riverbed play, with upstream sweetfish and birds near the weir. Seseragi Hall shares river information.

activities.name: Club Citta
activities.description: Large live hall in La Cittadella, five-minute walk from Kawasaki Station. Opened in 1988; Japanese and foreign artists perform.

activities.name: La Cittadella
activities.description: Italian hill-town entertainment complex a five-minute walk from Kawasaki Station, with movies, dining, shopping, and events.

activities.name: Kawasaki Factory Night View Houseboat Cruise
activities.description: Houseboat tour from Shiohama along canals to view factory nightscapes, with a navigator and shuttle bus.

activities.name: Todoroki Ryokuchi
activities.description: Sports park with track, baseball, tennis, soccer, and Todoroki Arena; the stadium is Kawasaki Frontale's home.

activities.name: Kawasaki Racecourse
activities.description: Popular night racing from April through December; last race around 8:50 p.m.

activities.name: Kashima Garden
activities.description: Sells traditionally dug pansies and violas; visitors may dig flowers. Also sells vegetables and offers harvests.

activities.name: Kawasaki Racecourse Barbecue Area
activities.description: A new barbecue plaza inside Kawasaki Racecourse with a large screen for races and playground equipment.

activities.name: Tamagawa Unane Park Golf
activities.description: Park golf, a golf-like sport for all ages and genders, at a low-fee facility owned by Kawasaki City.

activities.name: Kappa Park Saginuma (Saginuma Fureai Square)
activities.description: Children's play area with lawn, grassy field, and dirt ground zones.

activities.name: Sugo Green Space
activities.description: East area has slope athletics and large play equipment for children; west suits forest bathing and walks.

activities.name: Tokaraku Pottery Studio
activities.description: Pottery classroom in Kawasaki offering hand-building experiences, six minutes on foot from Musashi-Kosugi Station.

activities.name: Kureha Environment Wastec Kanagawa
activities.description: Kawasaki facility offering tours of waste intake, crushing, incineration, and residue treatment.

activities.name: Kawasaki Large-Scale Solar Power Plant
activities.description: Since 2011, about 100,000 panels produce up to 20,000 kW. Tours from Eco Mirai-kan include Haneda Airport views.

activities.name: Kawasaki Citizens Soap Plant
activities.description: Collects used cooking oil to make and sell recycled soap and biodiesel. Each manufacturing process can be toured.

activities.name: Minaminogawa Fureai Forest
activities.description: Woodland kept in its original natural state, with walking paths and benches for experiencing rich nature.

activities.name: Bornelund World of Play Grand Tree Musashi-Kosugi
activities.description: Fourth-floor indoor parent-child play area at Grand Tree Musashi-Kosugi with baby garden, large wooden equipment, and slide ball pool.

activities.name: FISH ON Ozenji
activities.description: Lure, fly, and bait ponds stock stream fish, with barbecue, dog run, cafe, and night facilities.

activities.name: Yumemigasaki Animal Park
activities.description: Free year-round Kawasaki municipal animal park on a hill, with about 50 species and a playground.

activities.name: Candy Cutting Experience
activities.description: Cut soft candy sticks at Matsuya Sohonten, the area's first candy shop on Kawasaki Daishi's shopping street.

activities.name: Kawasaki City Art Center
activities.description: Cultural promotion hub opened in 2007 in Shin-Yuri, housing a 195-seat theater and 113-seat screening hall.

activities.name: Muza Kawasaki Symphony Hall
activities.description: Opened in 2004 as a symbol of music-town Kawasaki, with vineyard seats praised for acoustics.

activities.name: Teatro Giglio Showa
activities.description: Comprehensive theater at Showa University of Music, with European tradition, advanced stage equipment, and natural acoustics.

activities.name: Kaguchi-no-ike and Keshomen-dani Park
activities.description: Cherry trees surround the pond; April blossom viewing is lively. The park can be enjoyed with children.

activities.name: Tachibana Onsen Tachibana-yu
activities.description: An onsen public bath with the latest facilities and a spacious, clean community space.

activities.name: Sakura Tobo Pottery Class
activities.description: Pottery class run by ceramic artist Michiko Kamo. Accepts orders for original pottery, gifts, favors and celebrations.

activities.name: Motoki Farm Strawberry Picking
activities.description: Strawberry picking January to mid-May, web reservations only. Nine varieties, direct sales and kids space, 7-minute walk from Kurokawa Station.

activities.name: Ozenji Furusato Park
activities.description: A park themed on water and greenery in the Tama Hills, with woodland paths and a Mt. Fuji viewing plaza.

activities.name: Yomiuriland
activities.description: Lush amusement park with thrill rides, bungee jumping, a Ferris wheel, character shows, and sea lion shows.

activities.name: Kawasaki Velodrome
activities.description: A 400m bank with a steep incline, plus a BMX and skateboard park opened in summer 2022.

activities.name: BOULCOM Kawasaki
activities.description: Bouldering gym for children and beginners, five minutes on foot from Kawasaki Station; no reservation needed.

activities.name: Miyamaedaira Gensen Yukemuri no Sho
activities.description: Day-trip natural onsen with carbonated amber baths, one of Kanto's largest bedrock baths, dining, and healing.

activities.name: Mizonokuchi Onsen Kirari
activities.description: Weakly alkaline bicarbonate day-trip onsen with an open-air beauty bath and free-flowing source spring.

activities.name: Sauna House
activities.description: Opened January 23, 2025. Six-story sauna house with five saunas per gender, cold and warm baths, restaurant, and relaxation.

activities.name: Kurokawa Sunflower Field Opening and Picking Experience
activities.description: Free no-reservation sunflower field opening and picking in Kurokawa, Kawasaki; schedule may change with growth.

activities.name: Yomiuriland Pool WAI
activities.description: Yomiuriland opens Pool WAI, a leading Tokyo leisure pool, from June 27 to September 23, 2026.

sights.name: Inage Shrine
sights.description: Kawasaki guardian shrine of victory and harmony, with a sacred ginkgo said to be over 1,000 years old.

sights.name: Kawasaki Daishi Heiken-ji
sights.description: Famous temple drawing many nationwide New Year visitors, known for warding off misfortune, with daily goma prayers.

sights.name: Kawasaki City Nihon Minka-en
sights.description: Twenty-five relocated eastern Japan folk houses, watermills, and a kabuki stage in Ikuta forest.

sights.name: Kawasaki City Fujiko F. Fujio Museum
sights.description: Cultural facility sharing manga artist Fujiko F. Fujio's works and messages through original art.

sights.name: Kawasaki City Greening Center
sights.description: Urban greening botanical garden offering seasonal plant displays, a greenhouse, and a lawn plaza for rest.

sights.name: Nikaryo Canal Kuji Cylindrical Diversion
sights.description: 1941 irrigation divider, a 1998 registered tangible cultural property, siphons under Hirase River, metering by cylinder angle.

sights.name: Taro Okamoto Museum of Art, Kawasaki
sights.description: Mostly underground museum fused with nature, centered on the Tower of Mother and experiential displays.

sights.name: Kawasaki Marien
sights.description: 51m port observation room, gym, tennis courts, and one of the world's largest great white shark specimens.

sights.name: Kawasaki River Port Water Gate
sights.description: Completed in 1928 on the Tama River, with a fruit-basket tower ornament; registered cultural property since 1998.

sights.name: Tokaido Kawasaki-juku Exchange Hall
sights.description: Exhibits on Kawasaki history and its Edo-period Tokaido post town, with costume photos and classical performances.

sights.name: Futago Shrine
sights.description: Near the Tama River's Futago Bridge; reportedly founded in 1641 as old Futago Village's shrine.

sights.name: Nitta Shrine
sights.description: Shrine enshrining Nitta Yoshisada, a famous general of the Kamakura period.

sights.name: Choja-ana Horizontal Cave Tomb
sights.description: Horizontal cave tombs cut into a hillside in the 7th-century Asuka period; interior entry is closed for safety.

sights.name: Hisamoto Yakuimon Park
sights.description: Former Oka family site, eight generations of doctors, said to model the sanatorium in Kurosawa's Red Beard.

sights.name: Suenaga Kumanomori Green Space (Edomi Cherry and Tarzan Tree)
sights.description: Mountain cherry found and put into verse by Minamoto no Yoshiie, later called Edomi Cherry, plus a Tarzan Tree.

sights.name: Kuji Plum Grove Park
sights.description: About 3,800 sqm with 40 plum trees of 20 species; red and white blooms mid-February to early March; poetry monument.

sights.name: Egawa Seseragi Promenade
sights.description: Eight themed zones with plants and stones; stream uses highly treated sewage water from Todoroki Water Treatment Center.

sights.name: Chidori Park
sights.description: Park built directly above Kawasaki Port undersea tunnel; observation plaza overlooks Higashi-Ogishima factory night views.

sights.name: Kotohira Shrine
sights.description: Old main hall burned in 2007; rebuilt in 2011 with restored paintings, after 1826 merger with Kotohira-gu.

sights.name: Shirahata Hachiman Shrine
sights.description: Said to be Genji-linked. Hatsu-u Festival has archery and a straw serpent; grand festival shows city-designated Negi dance.

sights.name: Tsukiyomi Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 1534 for harvest prayers; later became Aso Shrine, then Tsukiyomi Shrine again.

sights.name: Joraku-ji (Manga Temple)
sights.description: Main hall built around 1668-1703; nicknamed Manga Temple after manga drawn on sliding doors in 1968.

sights.name: Saimyo-ji
sights.description: Shingon temple revered by the shogun family; enshrines Daikokuten, one of Kawasaki's Seven Lucky Gods.

sights.name: Aso Fudo-in (Tokusa Fudo)
sights.description: Officially Myoozan Fudo-in Hannyabo, famous for a daruma market praying for health and family safety.

sights.name: Migawari Fudoson Kawasaki Head Temple
sights.description: Hall built to enshrine a miraculous image after an epidemic ended. Visitors pray year-round for evil-warding and traffic safety.

sights.name: Jokei-ji
sights.description: A hilltop temple known as Kakio's hydrangea temple, with over 1,000 hydrangeas and unique arhat statues.

sights.name: Hayano Sacred Park and Seven Ponds
sights.description: Seven ponds said to store spring water for fields. Cemetery and park preserve scenery; paths for observing plants and animals.

sights.name: Lord's Tomb
sights.description: Stone five-ring pagoda near Kaio-ji on Odoyama in Hayano, called the Lord's Tomb by locals.

sights.name: Sato Honjin Site
sights.description: Called Sozaemon Honjin, where 14th shogun Iemochi stayed en route to Kyoto; poet Sato Sonosuke born here in 1890.

sights.name: Kotoro Bridge Ruins
sights.description: Former drainage bridge; channel filled around 1931, only newel posts kept beside an intersection.

sights.name: Daishigawara Tidal Flat Museum
sights.description: Part of Daishigawara flood center; since 2008 shows Tama River estuary environment, history and culture, plus workshops and events.

sights.name: Basho's Haiku Monument
sights.description: Rare precious monument where poet Matsuo Basho, heading to Iga, composed a farewell haiku to disciples at Hatchonawate.

sights.name: Okamoto Kanoko Literary Monument: Pride
sights.description: 1962 Pride monument by son Okamoto Taro honoring poet-novelist Okamoto Kanoko.

sights.name: Togaku-in (Azalea Temple)
sights.description: Kawasaki temple known for about 2,000 azaleas, red and pink around Golden Week.

sights.name: Ishi Kannon Hall
sights.description: Tendai Meicho-ji's detached hall, opened in 1665 by monk Benyu; principal image is a stone Nyoirin Kannon.

sights.name: Kunikida Doppo Monument
sights.description: A monument inscribed with a famous poem by Japanese poet and novelist Kunikida Doppo.

sights.name: Shinshu-ji Kawasaki Cemetery Bell Tower
sights.description: Jodo Shinshu Honganji-ha temple bell tower with the Happiness Bell, painter Masuo Ikeda's posthumous work.

sights.name: Oishi Bridge
sights.description: In the Edo period a large stone bridge stood here, prospering as Mizonokuchi-Futago post town.

sights.name: Kamei Rokuro Residence Ruins
sights.description: Site of Kamei Rokuro's residence; descendants reportedly lived here until the early Showa period.

sights.name: Tachibana Ancient Hill Green Space
sights.description: Green space preserving Tachibana government-office ruins designated historic in March 2015; Nara-Heian early storehouses remain underground.

sights.name: Tachibana Shrine and Fujimidai Burial Mound
sights.description: Circular mound 17.5 meters across and 3.7 meters high; legend says Oto Tachibana Hime's robe and crown were buried here.

sights.name: Shiboguchi Shell Mound
sights.description: Prefecture-designated historic site; Tama Hills' oldest shell mound, about 7000 years old, type site for Shiboguchi pottery.

sights.name: Mizoguchi Shrine
sights.description: An ancient Kawasaki shrine enshrining Amaterasu, known for safe birth, child-rearing, matchmaking, and family safety.

sights.name: Kakio Local History Museum
sights.description: Opened in 2010 inside Kakio Junior High to exhibit history of former Kakio and Okagami villages.

sights.name: Sakuramoto Nine Lucky Gods
sights.description: Nine lucky-god statues installed on Sakuramoto shopping street in 1999, all facing upward, including a locally loved beckoning cat.

sights.name: Estuary Tidal Flats and Embankment Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: Tidal flats and reeds at the Tama River mouth, with embankment cherry blossoms.

sights.name: Midorigaoka Cemetery
sights.description: Northwestern Kawasaki cemetery where several hundred cherry trees bloom in spring.

sights.name: Kawasaki Sky and Greenery Science Museum (Planetarium)
sights.description: Learn about Kawasaki nature and enjoy a planetarium; new projectors show realistic stars, and binoculars are available.

sights.name: Kawasaki Port Undersea Tunnel
sights.description: Japan's longest walkable undersea tunnel, 2180 m by 3 m; pedestrian section opened 2004, links Chidori Park and Higashi-Ogishima.

sights.name: Mitutoyo Measurement Museum (Numata Memorial Hall and Measuring Instruments Hall)
sights.description: Museum of precision measuring instruments, comprising Numata Memorial Hall and Measuring Instruments Hall; holdings certified as Modern Industrial Heritage.

sights.name: Higashi-Ogishima East Park
sights.description: Kawasaki park with an artificial beach, popular for viewing planes, ships, and factory night views.

sights.name: Kawasaki City Environmental Research Institute

sights.name: Odawara Castle Ruins Park
sights.description: Castle ruins park with keep exhibits, observation deck, samurai and ninja halls, seasonal flowers, and an amusement park.

sights.name: Hotoku Ninomiya Shrine
sights.description: Shrine enshrining Ninomiya Sontoku, born in Odawara, who worked to revive farming villages in many regions.

sights.name: Ishigakiyama Castle
sights.description: Hideyoshi built a fully stone-walled castle in 1590 as his Odawara siege headquarters. National park area and national historic site.

sights.name: Odawara Castle
sights.description: National historic site; keep presents castle history and top deck overlooks Sagami Bay.

sights.name: Soga Shrine
sights.description: Said to be founded in 1028 by Soga Harima no Kami Yasuyoshi, enshrining Soga ancestors; Soga's main shrine since Meiji.

sights.name: Chokozan Shotai-ji
sights.description: About 360-year-old weeping cherry reportedly planted by Inaba Masanori, an Odawara City natural monument.

sights.name: Suzuhiro Kamaboko Museum
sights.description: Hands-on exhibits on fish cake history and nutrition, craftsman viewing, and making classes.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Museum of Natural History
sights.description: Museum of 4.6 billion years of natural science, with dinosaurs, a 2.5-ton meteorite, ammonites, and butterfly specimens.

sights.name: Odawara Literature Museum
sights.description: Exhibits materials on Odawara-born and associated writers in Tanaka Mitsuaki's Spanish-style villa.

sights.name: Former Matsumoto Gokichi Villa and Uko-tei Teahouse
sights.description: Politician Matsumoto Gokichi's villa, built around 1923: sukiya house, Uko-tei teahouse, garden with hill and water.

sights.name: Matsunaga Memorial Hall
sights.description: Founded in 1959 by Matsunaga Yasuzaemon, with historic buildings and a garden chosen among 100 historic parks.

sights.name: Soga Plum Grove
sights.description: Plum grove in Odawara with about 35,000 trees, the Odawara Plum Festival, and views of Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Odawara Blueway Bridge
sights.description: Bridge directly above Odawara Port, built using extradosed technology to secure the shipping lane below.

sights.name: Koki-an
sights.description: Yamagata Aritomo's Meiji villa, built at age 70, a masterpiece modern Japanese garden with Sagami Bay and Hakone borrowed scenery.

sights.name: Hojo Ujimasa and Ujiteru Graves
sights.description: Graves of fourth-generation Hojo Ujimasa and younger brother Ujiteru, where people wish with a happiness bell.

sights.name: Hojo Inari Shrine and Kawazuishi
sights.description: Said to have been built by the Hojo clan. Kawazuishi is a natural stone said to cry during Odawara crises.

sights.name: Sakawa River Open Levee
sights.description: Double levee letting water flow outside, unlike modern high levees. Also called Shingen Levee, reportedly devised by Takeda Shingen.

sights.name: Pine Avenue Associated with Ninomiya Sontoku
sights.description: About 400 black pines line the embankment to the river mouth, said planted by Ninomiya Sontoku.

sights.name: Kuno Kofun Group
sights.description: Leading late Kofun round tombs, about 120. Tombs 1, 2, 4, 15 remain; 4 and 15 chambers restored for visits.

sights.name: Odawara Flower Garden
sights.description: Botanical park with seasonal flowers, a tropical dome greenhouse, plum garden, rose garden, and iris pond.

sights.name: Anest Iwata Turnpike Hakone
sights.description: Scenic 9 m-wide ridge road: Hakone-Odawara 13.8 km and Hakone-Izu 1.7 km, open 5:30-22:30.

sights.name: Hoso-in Temple (Odawara Eight Lucky Gods / Jurojin)
sights.description: A temple enshrining Jurojin, one of the Odawara Eight Lucky Gods.

sights.name: Joei-ji
sights.description: A Nichiren sect temple in Shiroyama, Odawara City, Kanagawa Prefecture.

sights.name: Okubo Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Okubo Tadayo, who became Odawara Castle's first lord, and 11th-generation Tadamasa.

sights.name: Makino Shinichi Literary Monument
sights.description: Stone monument inscribed with a passage from a work by Odawara-born writer Makino Shinichi.

sights.name: Inoue Yasubumi Literary Monument
sights.description: Stone monument inscribed with a passage from Plum by Meiji-era Odawara poet Inoue Yasubumi.

sights.name: Komine Okane-no-dai Great Moat Cut
sights.description: Hojo dry moat severing the Hachimanyama ridge to the main keep, built against Hideyoshi.

sights.name: Densho-ji Temple
sights.description: Late Kamakura temple patronized by the Odawara Hojo, called Owl Temple for Kitahara Hakushu's writing house.

sights.name: Igami Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 1520 to enshrine Miura Yoshioki, last Miura warlord of Sagami, at Hojo Ujitsuna's wish.

sights.name: Daikyu-ji
sights.description: Temple built by Okubo Tadachika, Odawara castle lord and loyal retainer of Tokugawa Ieyasu.

sights.name: Hayakawaguchi Remains
sights.description: Part of Hojo defenses for the Odawara battle, facing Toyotomi headquarters, with double earthworks and moats.

sights.name: Hakushu Children's Song Museum
sights.description: Annex of Odawara Literature Museum in Tanaka Mitsuaki's nationally registered villa, showing Hakushu children's songs.

sights.name: Tokujo-in
sights.description: Temple with a deep history alongside castle-town Odawara, enshrining famous Great Buddha Enmei Jizo.

sights.name: Matsubara Shrine
sights.description: Odawara's chief guardian shrine, revered by successive castle lords since the Sengoku-period Odawara Hojo.

sights.name: Otemon Ruins
sights.description: Odawara Castle's main-gate ruins, relocated facing Edo in the Inaba period; bell rings at 6 a.m. and 6 p.m.

sights.name: Choon-ji (Odawara Eight Lucky Gods / Bishamonten)
sights.description: A Soto Zen temple in Odawara City, Kanagawa Prefecture, one of the Odawara Eight Lucky Gods.

sights.name: Odawara Castle Outer Fortifications
sights.description: Hojo defenses built for the Odawara campaign against Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Parts of the 9 km moats and earthworks remain.

sights.name: Renjo-in Earthwork
sights.description: Part of the Hojo outer defenses against Hideyoshi, valuable as a lowland site with Shibutori River as a moat.

sights.name: Sontoku Memorial Hall
sights.description: Memorial beside Ninomiya Sontoku's birthplace, exhibiting his life and teachings, with meeting and lodging rooms.

sights.name: Enpuku-ji (Odawara Eight Lucky Gods / Mizukake Hotei)
sights.description: To-ji Shingon esoteric temple in Odawara, one of the Eight Lucky Gods, reputedly founded over 400 years ago.

sights.name: Dairen-ji (Odawara Seven Lucky Gods / Fukurokuju)
sights.description: One of the Seven Lucky Gods centered on Odawara Castle; nearby temples allow a historic Odawara stroll.

sights.name: Rensen-ji (Odawara Eight Lucky Gods / Daikokuten)
sights.description: Nichiren temple in Odawara, one of the Eight Lucky Gods, founded by the Ide clan over 400 years ago.

sights.name: Odawara-juku Nariwai Exchange Hall
