sights.name: Tokiwagi Gate Samurai Museum
sights.description: Displays swords and armor, and offers dressing experiences as a samurai, princess, or ninja.

sights.name: Tsujimura Botanical Park
sights.description: 4.7 ha botanical park with foreign trees, about 350 plum trees, a picnic hill, and Sagami Bay views.

sights.name: Street Corner Museum (Odawara Station Umeboshi Museum)

sights.name: Hot Springs Research Institute

sights.name: Daijo-in

sights.description: Castle ruins park with a keep, observation deck, samurai and ninja halls, and seasonal flowers.

sights.name: Terugasaki Coast

sights.name: Oiso Shiroyama Park

sights.name: Former Residence of Shigeru Yoshida
sights.description: Stately Oiso sukiya-style mansion with vast gardens, a rose garden, and Mt. Fuji views on clear days.

sights.name: Oiso Guest House (Former Kinoshita Villa)

sights.name: Meiji Memorial Oiso Villa Garden

sights.name: Shigitatsu-an

sights.name: Jifuku-ji
sights.description: Shingon To-ji school temple in Oiso. Shimazaki Toson couple's grave among about 20 old plum trees blooming from early February.

sights.name: Shigitatsu-an
sights.description: Thatched-gate garden where Saigyo is said to have composed verse, and a cultural source of the word Shonan.

sights.name: Old Tokaido Pine Avenue (Oiso)

sights.name: Yokoku-ji Cave Tombs

sights.name: Former Shimazaki Toson Residence

sights.name: Kesho Well
sights.description: Said to be the makeup well of Tora-gozen, heroine of the Soga Monogatari, who lived in Oiso.

sights.name: Former Mitsui Villa District
sights.description: Site of a Meiji Mitsui zaibatsu head's villa, once with gardens and a national treasure tea room, now a park.

sights.name: Sawada Miki Memorial Hall (Hidden Christian Museum)

sights.name: Rokusho Shrine
sights.description: Ancient Oiso shrine jointly enshrining six major Sagami shrines; May 5 Konomachi festival.

sights.name: Takaku Shrine
sights.description: Stone monument by Tokugawa Yorimichi; main-hall plaque by Kabayama Sukenori. Edo daimyo reportedly dismounted to visit.

sights.name: Kewaizaka Pine Avenue
sights.description: Said to be Hiroshige's Oiso view, depicting rain of tragic love and a pine avenue.

sights.name: Kojima Honjin Ruins and Onoe Honjin Ruins
sights.description: Oiso post town, busy in the Edo period, had 66 inns and three honjin along about 1.3 km.

sights.name: Oiso Town Local History Museum

sights.name: Shiroyama Dam
sights.description: Dam in Sagamihara completed in 1965 for drinking and industrial water, power generation, and flood control.

sights.name: Sagami Dam
sights.description: Dam in Sagamihara City, completed in 1947 to secure water for supply, power generation, and irrigation.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Sagamihara Park
sights.description: Large lawn park beside Asamizo Park, with an iris garden, French-style formal garden, and tropical greenhouse.

sights.name: Miyagase Dam
sights.description: One of the capital region's largest concrete gravity dams, in eastern Tanzawa, northwestern Kanagawa, with six-minute tourist releases.

sights.name: Taimasan Park
sights.description: About 1,000 hydrangeas planted, a noted spot for Sagamihara City's flower. Best viewing in late June.

sights.name: Hirugatake Summit
sights.description: Kanagawa's highest peak: spring azaleas, golden larch foliage, summer constellations, and a 360-degree winter night panorama.

sights.name: Ogura Bridge and Sagami River Stream Walk
sights.description: Arched road bridge over the Sagami River, Shiroyama's symbol and civil engineering heritage, with summer lantern floating and illumination.

sights.name: Sagami Giant Kite Center (Renge no Sato Araiso)
sights.description: Japan's largest handmade kite, about 14.5 meters square and 950 kg, from a Sagamihara tradition since around 1830.

sights.name: Sagami River Fureai Science Museum Aquarium Sagamihara
sights.description: Aquarium displaying Sagami River creatures from upstream to the mouth, with feeding, keeper guides, and craft workshops.

sights.name: Ozaki Gakudo Memorial Hall
sights.description: Built in 1957 at Yukio Ozaki's birthplace, with photos, portraits, relics, and a Gakudo cherry tree.

sights.name: JAXA Sagamihara Campus (Space Science Exploration Exchange Building)
sights.description: JAXA space science visitor facility with an M-V rocket, satellite test models, Hayabusa2 exhibits, and guided tours.

sights.name: Obara-juku Honjin
sights.description: Only surviving official inn of Kanagawa's former 26, a grand pure-Japanese building designated a prefectural important cultural property.

sights.name: Komorebi Forest
sights.description: Enjoy seasonal nature on maintained paths and lawns; selected among Kanagawa's 50 beautiful forests.

sights.name: Kanuma Park
sights.description: A former reed marsh called Kanuma. Legend: giant Deirabotchi's footprint became the marsh. Carp, ducks, local rest spot.

sights.name: Seiryu no Sato
sights.description: Enjoy the Sagami River's rich nature and seasonal changes.

sights.name: Sagamihara City Old Folk House Garden
sights.description: Estimated mid-Edo Former Aoyagi-ji quarters, relocated and restored here, is a Kanagawa Prefecture Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Joshibi Art Museum (Joshibi University of Art and Design)
sights.description: Joshibi University Sagamihara campus museum with about six exhibitions, lectures, gallery talks, and workshops yearly.

sights.name: Kawajiri Stone Age Site
sights.description: Middle to late Jomon settlement site with varied artifacts and pebble-built remains, including stone-paved dwellings.

sights.name: Tsukui Castle Ruins
sights.description: Mountain castle built by reshaping Shiroyama, a major Sengoku-era Odawara Hojo border castle, now a prefectural park with trails.

sights.name: Katsusaka Ruins
sights.description: Restored Jomon pit dwellings, post-abandonment hollows, a stone-paved house replica, and on-site artifact displays.

sights.name: Lake Tsukui Shiroyama Park

sights.description: Observatory overlooks the Sagami River; a downstream riverbed plaza hosts sports and events.

sights.name: Hinokiboramaru

sights.name: Sagamihara North Park

sights.description: 55-meter observation tower in Sagamihara Asamizo Park overlooking Tanzawa, Tama Hills, and Yokohama.

sights.description: Former Koshu Kaido post-town inn rebuilt around 1897; city cultural property with sericulture and charcoal displays.

sights.name: Takada Bridge

sights.name: Mitsui Bridge

sights.name: Lake Miyagase

sights.name: Toriihara Garden

sights.description: Hidden panorama east of Shiroyama Lake; clear days show Landmark Tower, Tokyo Tower, and Skytree.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Sagamihara Park
sights.description: Park with early-blooming Harumeki cherries, a vast lawn, iris garden, formal garden, and greenhouse.

activities.description: Large windows offer close views of Minato Mirai, Bay Bridge, and Yokohama Port, plus full-course French dining.

activities.name: Daikoku Sea Fishing Facility
activities.description: Sea fishing park in Yokohama; adjoining green space overlooks Tokyo Bay. Reservations required on weekends, holidays, and busy periods.

activities.name: Nagayamon Park
activities.description: A 3.5-hectare park with spring water, cedar forest, thatched houses, a nagaya gate, and seasonal events.

activities.name: Children's Nature Park (Oike Park, Cherry Blossom Town)
activities.description: Large adventure playgrounds and a petting zoo with guinea pigs and mice. Spring cherry blossoms and excellent summit views.

activities.name: Wild Bird Observation Garden
activities.description: Year-round wild bird viewing from four windows, including kingfishers and ospreys.

activities.name: Niiharu Satoyama Park Exchange Center
activities.description: Donated former residence opened in 2009 as a rest place for nature observation and satoyama culture events.

activities.name: Jingashita Valley Park
activities.description: Only valley landscape in Yokohama, with trails for light trekking. Named for Yoritomo retainers' hunting camp.

activities.name: Sea Park
activities.description: Yokohama's only park with a swimming beach; clamming in early spring, swimming in summer.

activities.name: Yokohama Community Cycle baybike
activities.description: Borrow a bike in one place and return it in another, skipping purchase and parking rental.

activities.name: Kanazawa Nature Park
activities.description: One of Yokohama's largest nature parks, with a 100m roller slide, BBQ, and Boso Peninsula views.

activities.name: Nojima Park
activities.description: Park on Nojima in southernmost Yokohama, with observatory, BBQ, camping, and views of Fuji and Boso.

activities.name: Factory Night View Jungle Cruise
activities.description: Cruise to enjoy illuminated plants, tanks, and warehouses along the canal, aboard a luxury cruiser.

activities.name: Sky Spa Yokohama
activities.description: European-style spa and sauna directly connected to Yokohama Station, with view baths and a large sauna.

activities.name: Hamashin Yakatabune
activities.description: Yakatabune running from Yokohama Port and Tokyo, with three special boats for deck and night views plus Hayama beef kaiseki.

activities.name: Mitsuzawa Park
activities.description: Historic sports park opened in 1949, used for the National Sports Festival and Tokyo Olympics, with diverse sports facilities.

activities.name: Burari Nogeyama Zoo Bus
activities.description: Bus from Yokohama or Sakuragicho Station to the rare free Nogeyama Zoo, about 20 minutes from Yokohama.

activities.name: City Boundary Plaza
activities.description: A plaza on the Rokkoku Pass Hiking Course at the Kamakura City and Yokohama City border.

activities.name: Cat Cafe Reon
activities.description: Yokohama's first cat cafe, opened in 2008, with a separate room for nearly 30 cats and a cafe space.

activities.name: Gururi Rolled Sushi Class
activities.description: Specialized class teaching picture rolled sushi to children and people worldwide.

activities.name: Hama Rickshaw
activities.description: Rickshaw-based hospitality for Yokohama visitors and wedding guests, with support for local events.

activities.name: Renshinkan Kanto Regional Headquarters Imai Karate Dojo
activities.description: Ideal karate basics use symmetrical midline movements, breathing, and a focused shout to energize the whole body.

activities.name: TAIKO-LAB Shin-Yokohama
activities.description: One of the world's largest authentic taiko classes, plus a world-first fitness combining taiko striking with aerobic steps.

activities.name: Talk with Flowers Sogetsu-ryu Ikebana Studio fworks
activities.description: Find each flower's beauty and create your own ikebana while encountering Japan's seasonal flowers.

activities.name: Awazu Benibana Calligraphy School
activities.description: Large-brush calligraphy performances and hands-on sessions, short or in-depth, with Japanese, English, and Chinese simultaneous interpretation.

activities.name: Zounohana Terrace
activities.description: Opened in 2009, a rest house and art space in Zounohana Park hosting cultural programs and a cafe.

activities.name: Akaikutsu Sightseeing Loop Bus
activities.description: Retro loop bus evoking old streetcars, from Sakuragicho via the port, Red Brick Warehouse, Motomachi and Chinatown.

activities.name: Burari Sankeien Bus
activities.description: Links Yokohama Station East Exit to nationally designated garden Sankeien in about 35 minutes; stops at Sakuragicho and Chinatown.

activities.name: Cosmo Clock 21
activities.description: 112.5-meter clock Ferris wheel for 480, with 15-minute day panoramas and night views.

activities.name: Isho Kenkyukai
activities.description: Trains kimono tailors, sells creative kimono, and offers public sewing classes and silk pouch threading.

activities.name: Cycle Travelation
activities.description: Sports bike rental shop for Yokohama and Shonan, with cross bikes and road bikes.

activities.name: Kokonotsuido Suenosato Pottery and Glass Workshop
activities.description: Makes tableware and lights for the Kokonotsuido restaurant. Glassblowing and pottery experiences; on-site gallery sells works.

activities.name: Mugen-an
activities.description: Fourth-floor tea ceremony in a 4.5-mat room of a 1930 Yokohama historic building, originally a foreigner-only apartment.

activities.name: Yokohama Civic Disaster Prevention Center (Experience Facility)
activities.description: Yokohama's only hands-on disaster learning facility for quake shaking, initial firefighting, smoke escape, and simulations.

activities.name: Yokohama SUP Club
activities.description: SUP in Hinodecho, Yokohama, with careful instructor lessons on flat calm water for beginners and year-round events.

activities.name: Kiyoken Yokohama Factory
activities.description: About 90-minute tour of shumai and bento production, station-bento history, and a shop for fresh shumai.

activities.name: Yokohama Strawberry Park
activities.description: Reservation-only strawberry picking on weekends and holidays, renewed April 23, 2022, with a cafe.

activities.name: Maioka Park
activities.description: 28.5-hectare park of traditional valley scenery with wildlife, rice-farming events, a century-old farmhouse, and craft experiences.

activities.name: Shin-Yokohama Park (Grass Square)
activities.description: Vast grounds for skateboarding and running, with lawns and play equipment, a local relaxation spot.

activities.name: Yukata Dinner Cruise
activities.description: Self-chosen yukata night cruise in Yokohama; price includes new yukata, obi, and geta to keep. Summer only, reservation required.

activities.name: Yokohama Daisekai
activities.description: All-weather entertainment facility facing Tencho Gate in Yokohama Chinatown, with gift market, restaurants, cafe, and illusion-art museum.

activities.name: Asobiru
activities.description: Entertainment complex directly connected to Yokohama Station, with technology, crafts and kids themes for exciting nearby experiences.

activities.name: Honmoku Citizens Seaside Park
activities.description: Park with greenery and flowers, Hasshoden museum, D51 locomotive viewing, pottery, tennis, and baseball.

activities.name: Y Cruise Sea Bass Factory Night View Cruise
activities.description: Departs and arrives at Hammerhead; a guide shows night views of Minato Mirai, factories, and other facilities.

activities.name: BOATRACE Ticket Shop Boatpia Yokohama
activities.description: Off-track boatrace ticket hall with large-screen viewing, free seats, paid monitor seats, and VIP seats.

activities.name: Gumyoji Park
activities.description: Park on a hill near Keikyu Gumyoji Station, with a scenic observatory, plaza, and playground equipment.

activities.name: Kuroyu Natural Onsen Miura-yu Gumyoji
activities.description: Day-use facility with six natural onsen, six bath types, and two saunas for solo visitors or families.

activities.name: Shirahata Pond Park
activities.description: Quiet park near the station where people read on benches and children use playground equipment; a path circles the pond.

activities.name: Shiseido S/PARK
activities.description: Beauty experiences from science linking skin, body, and mind, only at Shiseido research: new food, cutting-edge items, and beauty checkups.

activities.name: Pacifico Yokohama
activities.description: Among the world's largest convention complexes overlooking Yokohama Port, a waterfront symbol with concerts, sports, and a seaside park.

activities.name: Reserved Cruise
activities.description: Luxury cruise viewing Yokohama scenery, with meals, drinks, and parties for two to about 100.

activities.name: Yokohama Arena
activities.description: One of Japan's largest multi-purpose halls for concerts, events, and corporate ceremonies.

activities.name: Yokohama Minato Mirai Hall
activities.description: Music hall in Minato Mirai, known for ocean views, a pipe organ, and 2,020 and 440 seats.

activities.name: Yokohama Night View Fantastic Cafe Ship
activities.description: Cafe ship cruise viewing Yokohama Three Towers, Bay Bridge, goddess statue, and Cosmo Clock 21.

activities.name: NISSAN STAR SUITES (Yokohama Stadium)
activities.description: Private viewing rooms on the fourth floor of Yokohama Stadium with balcony views of games.

activities.name: Pia Arena MM
activities.description: Concert arena opened in July 2020 with stage and seats close together.

activities.name: Yokohama Air Cabin
activities.description: Japan's first urban loop ropeway between Sakuragicho Station and Canal Park, with Minato Mirai views in about five minutes.

activities.name: Bayside Blue
activities.description: 18-meter matte metallic blue articulated bus for over 100, linking Yokohama Station, Minato Mirai, Yamashita, Chinatown and Red Brick Warehouse.

activities.name: Mulabo!
activities.description: Children's science experience center run by Murata, teaching electricity basics, with STEAM books, a cafe, and kids space.

activities.name: Anitouch Minatomirai
activities.description: Indoor contact facility by Izu Shaboten Animal Park with roughly 20 species and over 300 animals to touch and feed.

activities.name: Konica Minolta Planetaria Yokohama
activities.description: Japan's first LED dome planetarium offering fulldome healing shows, four premium seats, a cafe, and a gift shop.

activities.name: Kawasaki Super Factory Night View Cruise
activities.description: Ninety-minute rooftop cruise from Hammerhead viewing factory night illuminations, departing at 17:10 or 19:00.

activities.name: DREAM DOOR YOKOHAMA HAMMERHEAD
activities.description: Experiential outdoor theme park offering BBQ and glamping across three themed areas.

activities.name: Forest Adventure Yokohama
activities.description: Forest adventure next to Yokohama Zoo Zoorasia with kids, trek, and net courses, plus mountain biking.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Civic Hall Main Building
activities.description: Large cultural hall opened in 1975 overlooking Yokohama Port, hosting opera, pops concerts, and exhibitions.

activities.name: KAAT Kanagawa Arts Theatre
activities.description: Creative performing-arts theater opened in 2011 for musicals, plays, and dance, with changeable lighting and seating.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Youth Center
activities.description: Paid facilities include Momijizaka Hall (812 seats), Studio HIKARI (132 seats), and practice rooms.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Art Hall
activities.description: Art hall near the center of Hodogaya Park, opened in 1992 to support residents' arts activities.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Sports Hall
activities.description: Opened in January 1968 for sports promotion and health; renewed in April 1998 as a lifelong sports hub.

activities.name: Shinko Sports Kanagawa Prefectural Budokan
activities.description: Holds instructor training and martial arts classes; used for competitions and clubs, with a Japanese-style courtyard.

activities.name: Hodogaya Park
activities.description: Central Yokohama park with sports fields, an art hall, play equipment, and over 90 plum trees.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Shiki-no-Mori Park
activities.description: Woodland park in northwest Yokohama with firefly wetlands, rice paddies, iris garden, playground, and jumbo slide.

activities.name: InterContinental Yokohama Pier 8
activities.description: Hotel on Yokohama's Shinko Pier, sea on three sides, 173 rooms, two restaurants, guest spa, gym, courtyard, and rooftop.

activities.name: Center Minami Onsen Yumomi no Sato
activities.description: Golden carbonated onsen from 1800m underground, with a white foam bath, bedrock bath, dining, and healing.

activities.name: Kodomo no Kuni
activities.description: Nature-rich park opened in 1965, 30 km from central Tokyo, spanning Yokohama and Machida, with family play areas.

activities.name: Yokohama Yakatabune Seigi-maru
activities.description: Interior decorated in summer festival and cherry-blossom viewing style for a unique-venue program.

activities.name: Yokohama Hakkeijima Sea Paradise
activities.description: Japan's largest-class marine theme park with aquarium, attractions, shopping and a hotel; exclusive Live Stadium viewing in the Aqua Museum.

activities.name: Fantasy Kids Resort Kohoku
activities.description: Huge indoor facility with many attractions for babies through elementary-school children, playable in the rain.

activities.name: Hapipi Land Yokohama Asobiru Store
activities.description: Space-themed indoor kids theme park where children learn sense, sensibility, and intellect through play.

activities.name: Hapipi Land Lalala Kohoku Store
activities.description: Indoor play facility for safe family fun, with equipment nurturing children's hearts, bodies, and heads.

activities.name: Yokohama City Honmoku Civic Pool
activities.description: Main pool is a 240-meter flowing circuit, with a shallow shore pool and two slides.

activities.name: SMOKE DOOR Summer Indoor Beer Garden (Ended)
activities.description: Limited indoor beer garden at SMOKE DOOR in Hotel The Knot Yokohama, July 20 to August 31, 2025.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Mitsuike Park Pool
activities.description: Summer pool at Mitsuike Park: 25-meter pool, infant swamp and frog pools, a long slide, and water plaza.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Shiki-no-Mori Park Wading Pool
activities.description: Created on wooded rural hills, with a pond and a rocky stream for water play among trees.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Hodogaya Park Pool
activities.description: Five pools open in summer, including children's pools, a popular slider pool, and a 25m pool.

activities.name: Yokohama Fortune Aquarium
activities.description: Japan's only fortune-telling-themed aquarium on Yokohama Chinatown's main street, with auspicious fish for six fortunes.

activities.name: Y Cruise Marine Rouge
activities.description: Yokohama Port restaurant ship from Red Brick Warehouse, with French course meals and Bay Bridge and Minato Mirai views.

activities.name: Suishin Fruit Parlor Lab
activities.description: Experience cafe themed on fruit and sweets, with showy photogenic desserts and a Minato Mirai atmosphere.

activities.name: Unko Museum Yokohama Bay
activities.description: Indoor experience facility themed on poop love, with photo spots for families, friends, and couples.

activities.name: CAPCOMIX Minatomirai
activities.description: Capcom experience amusement facility opening summer 2026 at MARK IS Minatomirai, first in eastern Japan.

activities.name: Yokohama Marine Rocket
activities.description: Music-and-dance shows tell various stories without songs, with sign-language dance. Dine before the show; private bookings available.

sights.name: Ehrismann Residence
sights.description: Silk trader Ehrismann's 1926 home by A. Raymond, relocated to Motomachi Park in 1990.

sights.name: Osanbashi Yokohama International Passenger Terminal
sights.description: One of Japan's largest passenger terminals, with a lawn rooftop and views across Yokohama Port.

sights.name: Grand Mall Park
sights.description: Vast sea-themed open space in Minato Mirai 21 with zelkova trees, sea-motif benches, a lawn plaza and night views.

sights.name: Nihon-odori
sights.description: Japan's first Western-style street, designed by R.H. Brunton and completed around 1870, lined with historic buildings.

sights.name: Nippon Maru Memorial Park (Sailing Ship Nippon Maru and Yokohama Port Museum)
sights.description: Waterfront park with sailing ship Nippon Maru, a national Important Cultural Property called the Swan of the Pacific.

sights.name: Bluff No. 18
sights.description: Foreign residence built after the 1923 earthquake, later a church rectory, restored and opened in Yamate in 1993.

sights.name: Harbor View Park
sights.description: Overlooks Yokohama Bay Bridge; three rose gardens bloom in May and from mid-October to mid-November.

sights.name: Yokohama Minato Mirai 21
sights.description: Port-facing area of modern towers, malls, and hotels, with Landmark Tower, Red Brick Warehouse, and an aerial ropeway.

sights.name: Yokohama Landmark Tower
sights.description: Offices, hotel, and mall around the tower, plus a hall and Dockyard Garden; Sky Garden closed December 31, 2025.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Government Main Building
sights.description: Completed in 1928 and nicknamed King's Tower, this national Important Cultural Property is a representative modern building of Yokohama.

sights.name: Kishamichi Promenade
sights.description: Promenade from Sakuragicho across the sea on a former 1911 port railway into Minato Mirai.

sights.name: Gumyo-ji Kannon
sights.description: Yokohama's oldest temple, founded in 1044. Main hall rebuilt in 1766. Eleven-faced Kannon is a National Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Sankeien Garden
sights.description: Vast Japanese garden with relocated historic buildings and seasonal scenery, created by silk merchant Hara Sankei.

sights.name: Bashamichi
sights.description: Street in Yokohama named for foreign residents riding carriages; gas lamps and red-brick sidewalks remain.

sights.name: Biwajima Benzaiten
sights.description: Reportedly founded by Yoritomo's wife Hojo Masako, who built a sea island at Seto Shrine. Enshrines Benzaiten; Seaside Line view.

sights.name: Berrick Hall
sights.description: Built in 1930 as British trader B.R. Berrick's residence, the largest surviving prewar Yamate foreign house.

sights.name: Myoko-ji
sights.description: Said to have been founded in 652; its Kamakura-period bell is a prefectural Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Yamate House No. 111
sights.description: Built in 1926 for American Mr. Raffin, designed by J.H. Morgan, and open to the public since 1999.

sights.name: Yamate 234 Building
sights.description: Built around 1927 as apartments for foreigners, designed by Kichizo Asaka. Second floor now used for galleries and meetings.

sights.name: Yamate Italian Hill Garden
sights.description: Once home to the Italian consulate, hence Italian Hill. Geometric Italian flower beds, free Western houses, and hill views.

sights.name: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse
sights.description: Red-brick warehouses built from late Meiji to early Taisho, with cafes, shops, and harbor views.

sights.name: Yokohama Archives of History
sights.description: Holds about 270,000 Yokohama materials from Edo to early Showa; old building is the 1931 former British Consulate.

sights.name: Yokohama British House
sights.description: 1937 British consul-general residence with King George VI's arms. British-owned until 1969. Some interiors remain British-style.

sights.name: Yokohama Three Towers
sights.description: Prefectural Office (King), Yokohama Customs (Queen), Port Opening Memorial Hall (Jack), likened to playing cards by foreign sailors.

sights.name: Yokohama Customs
sights.description: Islamic-style dome marks the 51-meter Queen tower, tallest of Yokohama's three, completed in 1934.

sights.name: Gas Lamp Monument
sights.description: Japan's first gas lamps were installed in 1872; a replica was restored in 1986.

sights.name: Equine Museum of Japan
sights.description: Closed for renovation, reopening around 2029. Negishi, Japan's first full-scale racecourse site, has horse materials and a pony center.

sights.name: The Diplomat's House
sights.description: 1910 home of diplomat Uchida Sadatsuchi, designed by J.M. Gardiner, moved here in 1997; a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Former Ito Hirobumi Kanazawa Villa
sights.description: Thatched-roof building built in 1898 by first Prime Minister Ito Hirobumi in Nojima Park, overlooking Hakkeijima and the sea.

sights.name: Suzaki Shrine
sights.description: Historic shrine said to have been founded in 1191 by Minamoto no Yoritomo.

sights.name: Seto Shrine
sights.description: Sea deity since the 5th-6th centuries; Yoritomo invited the Izu Mishima deity, grateful for aid against the Taira.

sights.name: Soji-ji Temple
sights.description: One of two Soto Zen head temples; moved to Yokohama after a Meiji fire. Open grounds, zazen, and sutra copying.

sights.name: Namamugi Incident Monument and Site
sights.description: 1862 site where British merchants entering Shimazu Hisamitsu's procession were slashed, prompting the Anglo-Satsuma War.

sights.name: Silk Museum
sights.description: Museum introducing the silkworm-to-silk process, silk history, and kimono textile crafts, with live silkworms and workshops.

sights.name: Kamonyama Park
sights.description: Hilltop park in Nishi Ward overlooking Minato Mirai 21, with Ii Naosuke's statue and 200 cherry trees.

sights.name: Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum
sights.description: Recreates 1958 retro streets with select ramen shops. Learn ramen history, make custom cup ramen or noodles, and shop.

sights.name: Cup Noodles Museum Yokohama
sights.description: Hands-on food education on instant ramen, invention, and venture spirit, with workshops making Chicken Ramen and original Cup Noodles.

sights.name: Mitsubishi Minatomirai Industrial Museum
sights.description: Hands-on technology museum with real rocket engines and a full-scale Shinkai 6500 model, covering deep sea to space.

sights.name: Hara Model Railway Museum
sights.description: Museum showing Hara Shintaro's railway models, first tickets, and antique toys, highlighted by a huge diorama.

sights.name: Segami Citizens' Forest and Daimaru Plaza
sights.description: Forest in southern Yokohama; Daimaru Plaza is a rest spot for walks.

sights.name: Taya Caves (Josen-ji)
sights.description: Huge man-made cave at Josen-ji, said to date from the Kamakura period, about 570 meters long.

sights.name: Yokohama Park
sights.description: Yokohama's second oldest park after Yamate Park, famous for Yokohama Stadium and spring tulips.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Sakaigawa Retarding Basin Park
sights.description: First prefectural urban park coordinated with river works, using a lower Sakaigawa flood basin in normal times.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Kanazawa-Bunko Museum
sights.description: Warrior library founded by Hojo Sanetoki; a prefectural history museum since 1990.

sights.name: Ice Cream Origin Monument
sights.description: Japan's ice cream is said to have started on Bashamichi in 1869; statue installed in 1976.

sights.name: NYK Hikawa Maru
sights.description: A 1930 Seattle-route cargo-passenger ship moored by Yamashita Park, Japan's only surviving prewar example and a 2016 Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Iseyama Kotaijingu Shrine
sights.description: Yokohama's chief guardian shrine, enshrining Amaterasu and known as the Ise of the Kanto region.

sights.name: Machiya Shrine
sights.description: Oral tradition says Toyotomi retainers enshrined Gozu Tenno here after Osaka Castle fell and began the summer Gion festival.

sights.name: Monument to the Origin of Telephone Exchange
sights.description: Monument marking Japan's first telephone exchange, begun here in 1890 between Yokohama and Tokyo and within Yokohama.

sights.name: Miyagawa Kozan Makuzu Museum
sights.description: Compact housing for foreigners built around 1927, now open with Yamate 234 panels and gallery rental space.

sights.name: Ryuge-ji
sights.description: Ancient temple by Yoritomo and Mongaku in Kamakura's outer port, famed for senility-preventing Kannon, Muromachi Jizo, Daikoku, and peonies.

sights.name: Shomyo-ji
sights.description: Family temple of the Kanazawa Hojo, built in the Kamakura period, with a beautiful Jodo-style garden.

sights.name: Okurayama Memorial Hall
sights.description: Built in 1932 by Kunihiko Okura; a Yokohama City tangible cultural property and popular film location.

sights.name: Yamate Catholic Church
sights.description: A Christian Catholic church in Yokohama City, Kanagawa Prefecture.

sights.name: Yokohama Christ Church
sights.description: Anglican church founded in 1947, begun as the British church of the foreign settlement.

sights.name: Tsurumi Shrine
sights.description: Said to date from Emperor Suiko's reign, renamed in 1920, and called the oldest shrine between Kawasaki and Yokohama.

sights.name: Odori Park
sights.description: Over 1km park from JR Kannai south exit to subway Bandobashi, built on a filled canal in eight sections.

sights.name: Yokohama Rural Life Museum Misono Park Yokomizo Residence
sights.description: Front gate, main house and storehouses preserve the original scenery of Edo-period rural life, a precious cultural heritage.

sights.name: Yokohama Naritasan
sights.description: Branch of Chiba's Naritasan Shinshoji drawing many worshippers; goma rites pray for wishes before Fudo Myoo.

sights.name: Yokohama Street Art
sights.description: Artworks around Yokohama enjoyed with strolling and shopping, including Fruit Tree in Rinko Park and Grand Mall Park pieces.

sights.name: Minato Mirai Bridge
sights.description: Bridge linking the Portside and Minato Mirai districts, overlooking Bay Quarter, Sogo Yokohama, and the Katabira River Canal.

sights.name: Izumi River
sights.description: Waterside developed by Yokohama City for plum, cherry, hydrangea, autumn leaves, and birdwatching.

sights.name: Red Brick Park
sights.description: Historic green space centered on the Red Brick Warehouse, preserving customs ruins and a former station platform.

sights.name: France Bridge
sights.description: Named for French troops stationed from late Edo to early Meiji. 140m bridge linking Yamashita-cho with Motomachi and Yamate.

sights.name: Tsurumi Bridge Checkpoint Historic Site
sights.description: Historic checkpoint set up to control suspicious ronin after repeated attacks on foreigners following Yokohama's port opening.

sights.name: Yokohama Marine Tower
sights.description: Yokohama symbol built for the port-opening centenary. Reopened September 1, 2022, with nighttime light and image media art.

sights.name: Tennomori Izumikan (Former Shimizu Silk Mill Main Building)
sights.description: Main building of the Meiji-founded Shimizu Silk Mill, a Yokohama City designated historic building.

sights.name: Magokoro Farm
sights.description: Seasonal vegetables centered on tomatoes and long green onions have rich flavor and lasting freshness.

sights.name: Yokohama Doll Museum
sights.description: A doll museum with over 10,000 pieces from 140-plus countries, including Living National Treasure works, plus hands-on events.

sights.name: JOINUS Forest Sculpture Park
sights.description: Rooftop garden near Yokohama Station's west exit at JOINUS Yokohama, with about 20,000 trees, an artificial waterfall, and paths.

sights.name: Tokuzen-ji
sights.description: Notable for a fine wooden temple gate, with seasonal plants to view in the grounds.

sights.name: Hozo-ji
sights.description: A Shingon temple a 10-minute walk from Ayase Station.

sights.name: Zentsu-in Seishi-do
sights.description: Soto Zen temple. Seishi Bodhisattva was excavated after a dream. Main hall built in 1624-43 enshrines Jurojin.

sights.name: Yokohama Kanteibyo
sights.description: Yokohama Chinatown building enshrining Guan Yu, with a colorful dragon-motif tower gate.

sights.name: Hasseiden
sights.description: Built in 1933 by Home Minister Adachi Kenzo for spiritual cultivation; now a local history museum.

sights.name: Omaruyama (Kanazawa Citizens' Forest)
sights.description: From Yokohama's highest peak at 156.8 meters, views of Kanazawa Hakkei and Tokyo Bay.

sights.name: Yokohama Yamate Tennis Birthplace Memorial Hall
sights.description: Lawn tennis reached Yokohama in 1876 and was first played in Yamate Park. The 1998 hall displays tennis history.

sights.name: Former Yamate No. 68
sights.description: Built in 1934 as rental housing for foreigners at Yamate 68, later relocated and now the Yamate Park management office.

sights.name: Fujizuka Ruins (East of Yokone Inari)
sights.description: High ground with views of Mount Fuji, Oyama, the Tanzawa mountains, and the Hakone range.

sights.name: Yamate Museum
sights.description: Built in Meiji 42, Yokohama's only Japanese-Western wooden Western-style house, with exhibits on culture and customs since the port opening.

sights.name: Yatozaka Slope
sights.description: A slope along Harbor View Park cutting through valley-like terrain, linking Yamashitacho and Motomachi with hilltop Yamatecho.

sights.name: Nokendo Ruins
sights.description: Sekihitsuzan Jizoin rebuilt by lord Kuze Hiroyuki in 1661-73; poems here began the Kanazawa Eight Views.

sights.name: Fudo Pond
sights.description: Quiet small pond in Nokendo Green Space, said to be visited by kingfishers and other birds.

sights.name: Yatsu Sekigaya Fudoson
sights.description: Fudo long revered by villagers; the precinct waterfall is the source of the Yatsu River.

sights.name: Kamariya Citizens' Forest
sights.description: Simple natural mixed woodland where large trees still remain.

sights.name: Nissan Global Headquarters Gallery
sights.description: Gallery of Nissan, founded in Yokohama in 1933, with latest cars and heritage displays.

sights.name: Osaragi Jiro Memorial Museum
sights.description: Introduces Yokohama writer Osaragi Jiro, south of Harbor View Park's observatory.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Museum of Modern Literature
sights.description: Museum, library, and lecture hall for Kanagawa-linked writers including Natsume Soseki and Akutagawa Ryunosuke.

sights.name: Nissan Engine Museum
sights.description: Displays 28 of about 200 Nissan engines in a 1934 building later designated modern industrial heritage.

sights.name: Yokohama Local Meteorological Observatory
sights.description: 1927 office renovated in 2007 to a Tadao Ando design, with seismic reinforcement and a new second building.

sights.name: Yokohama City Tram Museum
sights.description: Preserves seven tram cars, stop signs, and paving stones; opened in 1973 and rebuilt in 1983.

sights.name: Dockyard Garden
sights.description: Japan's oldest existing stone dock for merchant ships, restored beside Landmark Tower for concerts and promotions.

sights.name: Hokubu Daini Water Reclamation Center
sights.description: East of the Tsurumi River estuary, treating Tsurumi Ward's Tokyo Bay side nonstop since 1984.

sights.name: Tsurumi River Embankment
sights.description: From the riverside path and embankment, watch waterbirds, photograph trains and the Shinkansen, and see Mount Fuji on clear days.

sights.name: Zounohana Park Yamashita Rinko Line Promenade Viaduct
sights.description: About 500-meter promenade linking near Yokohama Customs, via Osanbashi entrance, to Yamashita Park's west end, built reusing the old line.

sights.name: Yokohama English Garden
sights.description: English garden centered on about 2,200 rose varieties, with a rose tunnel, six areas, a cafe, and a shop.

sights.name: Sandendai Ruins and Archaeology Museum
sights.description: Jomon, Yayoi and Kofun village ruins on a 55-meter hill in Okamura, Yokohama, designated a national historic site in 1966.

sights.name: Yamate Park
sights.description: Japan's first Western-style park, created for foreign residents and famous as where tennis was first played in Yokohama.

sights.name: Augusta Milk Farm
sights.description: Yokohama farm offering cow milk, rich soft-serve, over 50 gelato flavors, and cow contact.

sights.name: Yamashitacho Park
sights.description: Park in Yokohama Chinatown with Chinese-style arbor Kaihotei and lion monuments in an exotic setting.

sights.name: Tokozen-ji
sights.description: Temple over 800 years old. Zazen and sutra copying by reservation; beginners guided; English zazen explanations available.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Museum of Cultural History
sights.description: Museum of Kanagawa culture and history one minute from Bashamichi Station; its neo-baroque wing is a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Ooka River Promenade
sights.description: 3.5 km Ooka River promenade with about 350 cherry trees, a leading Yokohama blossom spot, lantern-lit in bloom season.

sights.name: Yokohama Mazu Temple
sights.description: Enshrines Mazu, goddess of safe voyages, health and peace, and matchmaking god Gekka Rojin, in Chinese-style decor.

sights.name: Rinko Park
sights.description: Minatomirai's largest green space, with lawn plaza, south plaza, and tidal pond, overlooking Yokohama Port.

sights.name: Nojima Park Observatory
sights.description: Observatory atop Nojima Mountain with 360-degree views of Yokohama's sea, the Boso Peninsula, and Mt. Fuji.

sights.name: Negishi Natsukashi Park Former Yanagishita Residence
sights.description: Restored modern Japanese-Western house open to the public; Yokohama City tangible cultural property since 2002.

sights.name: Yokohama Foreign General Cemetery
sights.description: Began by burying Perry fleet sailors; now over 5,000 foreigners from about 40 countries, including noted figures in Japan's Westernization.

sights.name: Shirahata Migawari Jizo
sights.description: Jizo called Migawari after robbers beheaded it by mistake while young brothers hid behind it; locally revered.

sights.name: Honmoku Shrine
sights.description: Shrine known for matchmaking and evil-warding prayers; exhibition hall for prefecture-designated O-uma-nagashi ritual.

sights.name: Sogo Museum of Art
sights.description: Unprecedented full-scale museum in a department store holding Shintaro Suzuki oils, with domestic and overseas painting and sculpture exhibitions.

sights.name: Motomachi Hyakudan Park
sights.description: Park symbolized by a giant cherry tree; named for the 101-step Hyakudan stairs destroyed in the Great Kanto Earthquake.

sights.name: Yokohama Municipal Children's Botanical Garden
sights.description: About 3.0 ha park opened in 1979 for the International Year of the Child, with many gardens and rare varieties.

sights.name: Kodozan Honbutsuden
sights.description: Buddhist temple atop Mount Kodo overlooking Yokohama and Minato Mirai, with 250 spring cherry trees and a two-story reliquary pagoda.

sights.name: Keikyu Museum
sights.description: Opened in 2020 at Keikyu Group headquarters, showing Deha 230, a line diorama, driving simulation, and crafts.

sights.name: BankART Station
sights.description: Core BankART1929 space under Shin-Takashima Station for exhibitions, a shop, cafe, pub, and school.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Archives
sights.description: Collects and preserves prefectural public records and old documents, and holds exhibitions and lectures.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Plaza for Global Citizenship
sights.description: Facility for children's sensibility, global citizenship, and international activities, with exhibition rooms, a library, and events.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Music Hall
sights.description: Modernist hall by Kunio Maekawa, opened in 1954, with all-wood walls and acclaimed acoustics.

sights.name: Yokohama Marine Tower
sights.description: Yokohama symbol built in 1961 as a port centennial project, once Japan's tallest lighthouse, with about 90-meter observation floors.

sights.name: Okurayama Park
sights.description: Plum grove of 46 varieties and Okurayama Memorial Hall, a designated tangible cultural property.

sights.name: Kanagawa Prefectural War Dead Memorial Hall
sights.description: 1953 hall mourning war dead since the Meiji era, with views, cherry blossoms, and azaleas.

sights.name: Yokohama Museum of Art
sights.description: Large art museum with symmetrical exterior, open Grand Gallery, nine rooms, atelier, and library of about 240,000 books.

sights.name: Tulips at Yokohama Park
sights.description: Yokohama's second-oldest park after Yamate Park, famous for Yokohama Stadium and colorful spring tulips.

sights.name: Mystery of Tutankhamen: Immersive Ancient Egypt Exhibition
sights.description: Permanent immersive Tutankhamen exhibition at Yokohama Minato Mirai's Tutankhamen Museum (PLOT48).

sights.name: Minato Mirai Sakura Street Cherry Blossoms
sights.description: Roughly 100 Someiyoshino cherries line 500 meters from Sakuragicho Station to Landmark Tower and Pacifico Yokohama, a popular blossom spot.

sights.name: Roses of the Yamate Italian Hill Garden
sights.description: Park called Italian Hill for its former Italian consulate, with a geometric Italian garden and seasonal flowers.

sights.name: Hamagin Children's Space Science Museum
sights.description: Hands-on science museum featuring the world's best starry sky, designed as a giant spaceship with five themed exhibition rooms.

sights.name: CRAFT. BankPark YOKOHAMA
sights.description: City-designated historic former Dai-ichi Bank Yokohama Branch, built in 1929, used for exhibitions, launches, and filming.

day_to_day.name: Sukanagosso Produce Market
day_to_day.description: JA Yokosuka Hayama produce shop with fresh vegetables, Hayama beef, and popular Sekiguchi Ranch soft serve.

day_to_day.name: Yokosuka Dobuita Street
day_to_day.description: Shopping street blending American and Japanese culture where many shops accept US dollars.

day_to_day.name: Cainz Yokosuka Kurihama Store
day_to_day.description: Original Cainz brand offers interiors, daily and household goods, pet supplies, gardening, DIY, bicycles, and renovations.

day_to_day.name: Yokosuka Navy Curry Shop
day_to_day.description: An antenna shop offering a navy curry restaurant, retort curry, sweets, and Yokosuka souvenirs.

day_to_day.name: Wakamatsu Market
day_to_day.description: About one minute from Yokosuka-Chuo Station, some 70 Showa-retro bars, birthplace of the Yokosuka Brassiere cocktail.

day_to_day.name: Honey Bee
day_to_day.description: Shop serving the 100% beef Yokosuka Navy Burger with authentic American taste.

day_to_day.name: Restaurant Tsunami
day_to_day.description: On Yokosuka's Dobuita Street, serves Navy Burger, navy curry, and cherry cheesecake.

day_to_day.name: Gyoran-tei
day_to_day.description: Shop serving Yokosuka Navy Curry, a retro navy dish.

day_to_day.name: Yokosuka Port Market
day_to_day.description: Market and food court near Mikasa Park with Miura Peninsula foods, ocean-view dining, and live events.

day_to_day.name: HONEYBEE
day_to_day.description: Casual cafe serving sweets and light meals, popular for lunch and tea.

day_to_day.name: Mercure Yokosuka Bistro Bourgogne
day_to_day.description: High-floor full courses with Miura ingredients. Sea views of Yokohama and warships, wine, breakfast, lunch and dinner; non-guests welcome.

activities.name: YOKOSUKA Naval Port Cruise
activities.description: A roughly 45-minute local cruise to see US Navy and Maritime Self-Defense Force ships up close.

activities.name: Uraga Ferry
activities.description: Ferry linking east and west Uraga Port, nicknamed ponpon boat. Three-minute rides view former shipyard cranes and docks.

activities.name: Tokyo Bay Ferry
activities.description: Links Kurihama, Kanagawa and Kanaya, Chiba in about 40 minutes, with views of ships and Mount Fuji.

activities.name: Kurihama Flower Park
activities.description: Closed for now after typhoon damage. Free park with poppies, cosmos, herb garden, and adventure land.

activities.name: Kurihama Flower Land Pool
activities.description: Indoor heated pool enjoyable by adults and children, also with a training room.

activities.name: Mount Takatori
activities.description: Yokosuka mountain nicknamed Shonan Myogi, known for sheer vertical rocks, where you can hike.

activities.name: Tokyo Bay Ferry Terminal
activities.description: About a 40-minute ferry from Kurihama to Kanaya across Tokyo Bay, with southern Boso views.

activities.name: Kayama Farm Strawberry Picking Experience
activities.description: Soil-grown strawberries with organic fertilizer; pick Benihoppe and Tochiotome from early January to early June; daifuku and jam sold.

activities.name: Seaside Bath and Fisherman's Cuisine Yokosuka
activities.description: 850-seat ocean-view facility in Kurihama Port for fresh seafood, banquets, bathing, rest, and shopping.

activities.name: Tatara Beach
activities.description: One of the few white-sand beaches on the Miura Peninsula. Original Godzilla appeared here in 1954; footprints remain.

activities.name: Maeda River Promenade
activities.description: A clean 1.4 km stream walk with trees, birds, and aquatic life; part of a beginner hike. Partly closed.

activities.name: Kanagawa Prefectural Kannonzaki Park
activities.description: Vast park covering most of Kannonzaki on Tokyo Bay, with hydrangeas, forest walks, barbecue and Japan's first Western-style lighthouse.

activities.name: Heiwa Central Park
activities.description: Yokosuka rest park for praying for peace, with Tokyo Bay views and a monument beaming light 16 times a year.

activities.name: Sano Natural Onsen Noborigumo
activities.description: Sodium chloride natural onsen from 800 meters underground, called a beauty spring, with bedrock baths and a rock salt sauna.

activities.name: Beach Park Living
activities.description: Barbecue facility in Kannonzaki Park Tatarahama overlooking Tokyo Bay, serving domestic meat; 2022 Good Design Award winner.

activities.name: Tsukuihama Tourist Farm
activities.description: Strawberry, mandarin, and sweet potato picking; seasonal vegetables sold at the information office.

activities.name: Yokosuka Onsen Yura-no-Sato
activities.description: Salty seawater-like spring that moisturizes and stays warm, called a heat bath. Includes open-air bath and runner's spa.

activities.name: Yokosuka Natural Onsen Umibe-no-Yu Kurihama
activities.description: Sister shop of a Futtsu facility beside Kurihama ferry port. Open-air bath views Tokyo Bay and the Boso Peninsula.

activities.name: Touch Uocchi Aquarium, Soleil Hill
activities.description: Experience aquarium opening April 25, 2025 at Soleil Hill, gathering 12 aquatic species to touch or feed.

activities.name: Tondemi Yokosuka
activities.description: Indoor athletic facility with trampolines, climbing, and digital content; night illumination from 19:00.

activities.name: Mynavi Japan Cup Yokosuka
activities.description: Ended for 2025. Free freestyle BMX performances with music and an MC.

activities.name: Nagahama Beach
activities.description: Relaxed beach locals call Nahama, suited to families and snorkeling, popular for year-round marine sports.

activities.name: Yokosuka City Umikaze Park
activities.description: Park facing Sarushima with barbecues, sports facilities, playground equipment, and Third Sea Fort remains.

activities.name: #Jihangun Yokosuka
activities.description: Photo spot at Nobi Beach with vending-machine objects and a six-meter swing against sky and sea.

activities.name: Yokosuka YY Vehicle Festival 2026
activities.description: Ended event enjoying Yokosuka through JR East and Keikyu trains, JMSDF Yokosuka ships, and cars.

food.description: Bread and Western confectionery in Yokosuka.

sights.name: Kannonzaki
sights.description: A cape at Yokosuka's eastern end maintained as a park, with a lighthouse, battery ruins, museums, and year-round walks.

sights.name: Kannonzaki Lighthouse
sights.description: Japan's first Western-style lighthouse in Kannonzaki Park, overlooking Tokyo Bay and the Boso Peninsula.

sights.name: Kinugasayama Park
sights.description: Yokosuka park chosen among 100 cherry spots, with about 2,000 trees, a festival, and night lighting.

sights.name: Tateishi Park
sights.description: Known for Tateishi, a large odd rock on the coast, and views of it with Mount Fuji at sunset.

sights.name: Hashirimizu Water Source Park
sights.description: Cherry-blossom spot in Yokosuka overlooking Tokyo Bay, birthplace of the municipal water supply, with drinkable spring water.

sights.name: Hashirimizu Shrine
sights.description: Shrine dedicated to Yamato Takeru and Ototachibana-hime.

sights.name: Kano Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Higashi-Uraga, Yokosuka, whose inner-sanctum stairs, Enishi and Musubi slopes, are said to bless matchmaking.

sights.name: Tsukayama Park
sights.description: One of the oldest prefectural parks, overlooking Yokosuka Port, with about 800 cherry trees.

sights.name: Verny Park
sights.description: French-style park overlooking the former Yokosuka Ironworks site, with about 1,300 roses of 130 varieties.

sights.name: Sarushima Island
sights.description: Tokyo Bay's only natural island and largest uninhabited island, once a fortress with battery and barracks ruins.

sights.name: Memorial Ship Mikasa
sights.description: 1902 British-built battleship in Mikasa Park, Yokosuka; Russo-Japanese War flagship with onboard exhibits and VR.

sights.name: Awashima Shrine
sights.description: Worshipped as a shrine for matchmaking, safe childbirth, and the blessing of children.

sights.name: Kaigan Garden
sights.description: Tokyo Bay and Boso views; rare plants; Japan's first Western-style lighthouse, Meiji-era battery ruins, old powder magazines.

sights.name: Hashirimizu Kannonzaki Promenade (Boardwalk)
sights.description: About 600-meter promenade for leisurely walks viewing the sea; boardwalk for early-morning sunrise from the sea.

sights.name: Observation Garden
sights.description: Seaside viewpoint by Kannonzaki Park Center for ship watching; clear days show Yokohama Landmark Tower and Tokyo Skytree.

sights.name: Perry Park and Memorial Hall
sights.description: Park marking Perry's landing, with monument, memorial hall, historical materials and dioramas; July Kurihama Perry Festival venue.

sights.name: Yokosuka Museum of Art
sights.description: Art museum at scenic Kannonzaki reopening in September 2026, with exhibitions, unique architecture, views, and an Italian restaurant.

sights.name: Dokuen-ji
sights.description: Temple built about 400 years ago for repose of souls; zazen and sutra copying draw visitors from afar.

sights.name: Kurihama Port
sights.description: Port in eastern Yokosuka, Kanagawa, known as the place where Perry's forces landed.

sights.name: Cliff-carved Buddha
sights.description: Giant Maitreya Buddha carved on Mount Takatori by Shigeru Fujishima from 1960; about 8 m tall and 4.5 m wide.

sights.name: National Route 134
sights.description: National highway from Yokosuka to Oiso with views of the Shonan coast and Mount Fuji.

sights.name: Kannonzaki Nature Museum
sights.description: Exhibits mainly Tokyo Bay creatures. A popular touch pool lets you touch sea life from around Kannonzaki.

sights.name: Kasuya no Mori Contemporary Art Museum
sights.description: Private contemporary art museum opened in April 1994, with a tea lounge surrounded by a bamboo grove.

sights.name: Mabori Coast
sights.description: Seawall completed in 2006 after typhoon flooding. Its path is a palm-lined promenade for jogging, walks, and clear-weather Fuji views.

sights.name: Verny Memorial Museum
sights.description: Preserves and displays the Important Cultural Property steam hammer imported to late-Edo Yokosuka Ironworks.

sights.name: Gimeizan Mansho-ji
sights.description: Rinzai Zen temple founded in 1194 by Minamoto no Yoritomo for Miura Yoshiaki; reservation required.

sights.name: Shiroaka Inari Shrine
sights.description: More than 50 vermilion torii line the grounds, a rare Miura Peninsula landscape; kerria and hydrangeas bloom in spring.

sights.name: Uraga Community Center Annex (Local History Museum)
sights.description: Community space for lectures and events that also displays Uraga local history materials.

sights.name: Mikasa Park
sights.description: Representative Yokosuka park with a Togo Heihachiro statue, gateway to memorial ship Mikasa and Sarushima.

sights.name: Army Pier
sights.description: A park overlooking historic Uraga Port, scene of Perry's arrival and the Kanrin Maru's departure, near a ferry landing.

sights.name: Tomyodo
sights.description: Historic site of the Edo-period beacon at Uraga Port entrance and surrounding coast, used about 220 years until 1872.

sights.name: Yokosuka Modern Heritage Museum Tibodie House
sights.description: Recreated 150-year-old Western house of a French ironworks engineer in Verny Park.

sights.name: Yokosuka Iris Garden
sights.description: Iris garden at the foot of Mount Ogusu with over 400 varieties and about 140,000 plants.

sights.name: Taura Plum Village
sights.description: The Miura Peninsula's only plum grove, where over 2,000 plum trees bloom in February alongside daffodils.

sights.name: Tenjin Island Seaside Nature Education Garden
sights.description: A rare natural Miura Peninsula coast, designated a Kanagawa natural monument and scenic spot, with Fuji views.

sights.name: Otsu Suwa Shrine
sights.description: Otsu's guardian shrine founded in 824 from Suwa Taisha and rebuilt after the Great Kanto Earthquake.

sights.name: Joraku-ji
sights.description: Viewing resumed September 1, 2025. Ancient Ashina temple with five Unkei statues, national Important Cultural Properties.
